requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term MUST using BCP 14 when it appears in capitals.
requirements.rationale: The quoted MUST is one of the BCP 14 vocabulary definitions; this sentence defines terminology and imposes no publisher action.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term MUST NOT using BCP 14 when it appears in capitals.
requirements.rationale: The quoted MUST NOT introduces the BCP 14 prohibition vocabulary rather than prohibiting any protocol behavior.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term REQUIRED as BCP 14 mandatory language.
requirements.rationale: REQUIRED appears only in the quoted BCP 14 word list here; its normalized strength does not make the definition a runtime requirement.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term SHALL as BCP 14 mandatory language.
requirements.rationale: This quoted SHALL defines a BCP 14 synonym for MUST without identifying an endpoint operation.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term SHALL NOT as BCP 14 prohibition language.
requirements.rationale: SHALL NOT is mentioned as a BCP 14 synonym in the terminology paragraph; no publisher behavior is prohibited by this occurrence.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term SHOULD as BCP 14 recommendation language.
requirements.rationale: The BCP 14 vocabulary list quotes SHOULD to explain normative notation, without recommending a concrete protocol action.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term SHOULD NOT as BCP 14 negative recommendation language.
requirements.rationale: The quoted SHOULD NOT defines BCP 14 language and does not identify a discouraged publisher operation.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term RECOMMENDED as the BCP 14 synonym for SHOULD.
requirements.rationale: RECOMMENDED is a quoted vocabulary item in the BCP 14 declaration, not a recommendation to implement a feature.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term NOT RECOMMENDED as the BCP 14 synonym for SHOULD NOT.
requirements.rationale: This mention of NOT RECOMMENDED explains BCP 14 terminology; it supplies no discouraged runtime behavior.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term MAY as BCP 14 permission language.
requirements.rationale: MAY is quoted to define the BCP 14 vocabulary, so this occurrence grants no particular publisher capability.

requirements.summary: Interpret the quoted term OPTIONAL as the BCP 14 synonym for MAY.
requirements.rationale: OPTIONAL completes the quoted BCP 14 word list; it does not designate a protocol feature as optional here.

requirements.summary: Keep the previous Type plus Delta Type within 2^64 - 1 when encoding Key-Value-Pairs.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint emits Key-Value-Pairs in control and data messages. The harness can decode consecutive types using a wider sum and detect overflow independently of the receiver error rule.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a received Delta Type whose sum with the previous Type exceeds 2^64 - 1.
requirements.rationale: The receive rule applies to an endpoint acting as publisher as well as to a subscriber. A malformed control Key-Value-Pair sequence can trigger a deterministic session close.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a Key-Value-Pair value length exceeds 2^16 - 1 bytes.
requirements.rationale: For odd Types the preceding paragraph sets the value-length limit to 65535. A relay peer can send a declared length of 65536 to a publishing endpoint and observe its termination code.

requirements.summary: Close the session with KEY_VALUE_FORMATTING_ERROR when an understood Type's Value or Length/Value violates that Type's serialization.
requirements.rationale: A publisher also receives control Key-Value-Pairs. This check requires a Type the publisher understands and a malformed serialization, rather than an unknown Type or merely an invalid semantic value.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a Reason Phrase Length greater than 1024 bytes.
requirements.rationale: A relay can reject a publisher request with an oversized declared reason phrase. The maximum from the preceding lines and the mandated close code give a wire-visible boundary test.

requirements.summary: Render namespace tuple fields in order, separated by single hyphens.
requirements.rationale: This recommendation governs a publisher application's textual rendering for logging, filenames, or authorization. MOQT carries binary fields, so a relay-side protocol harness cannot observe this delimiter choice.

requirements.summary: Separate the last rendered namespace field from the track name with a double hyphen.
requirements.rationale: The track-name delimiter is an independently checkable part of the recommended text format, but it is not transmitted as that text by MOQT. No standard relay interaction exposes the application's rendering.

requirements.summary: Render bytes a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and underscore literally in serialized namespace and track names.
requirements.rationale: The recommendation covers literal output in an application-level name representation. Observing the binary Full Track Name cannot distinguish this rendering from an equivalent local spelling.

requirements.summary: Render every other name byte as a period followed by exactly two lowercase hexadecimal digits.
requirements.rationale: The escape form is prescribed for local serialized names. The relay sees decoded bytes, not the publisher's logging, filename, or authorization string, so this formatting advice has no deterministic protocol oracle.

requirements.summary: When parsing serialized names, enforce the rule that hexadecimal letters after a period are lowercase and reject uppercase hexadecimal letters.
requirements.rationale: The lead-in MUST governs the first canonicalization bullet. A publishing implementation that parses such names is covered, but the textual parser is outside the binary relay-facing MOQT interface.

requirements.summary: When parsing serialized names, reject escaped encodings of bytes that must appear literally.
requirements.rationale: The lead-in MUST also governs the distinct redundant-escape rule. The relay cannot supply serialized-name text through binary Track Namespace or Track Name fields to test this local parsing obligation.

requirements.summary: When parsing serialized names, require exactly two hexadecimal digits after every period.
requirements.rationale: The third bullet imposes an escape-width rule independently of letter case or redundant encoding. Its input is a textual application representation, which the relay-side protocol harness cannot exercise.

requirements.summary: Require hexadecimal letters a-f, rather than A-F, in period escapes in serialized names.
requirements.rationale: This MUST specifies the lowercase canonical form; numeric hexadecimal digits remain valid. A publisher's local string parser is covered conditionally, but its representation is not exposed on the MOQT wire.

requirements.summary: Fail serialized-name parsing when an escape contains uppercase hexadecimal letters A-F.
requirements.rationale: This occurrence explicitly requires parser failure for uppercase hexadecimal letters, separate from merely defining the valid spelling. Binary name fields cannot carry this local parser stimulus.

requirements.summary: Do not accept hexadecimal escapes for name bytes a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or underscore that have a literal representation.
requirements.rationale: MUST NOT wraps across lines 737-738 and prohibits redundant textual encodings such as .61. It applies to serialized-name handling, not to binary protocol names, and is not observable by the relay harness.

requirements.summary: Reject redundant escaped spellings of bytes with a literal serialized-name representation.
requirements.rationale: The explicit parser-rejection sentence reinforces the preceding prohibition. The contribution publisher may have such an application parser, but a relay cannot determine how its binary name bytes were spelled locally.

requirements.summary: Require every period in a serialized name to introduce exactly two hexadecimal digits.
requirements.rationale: The parser must reject a trailing period and incomplete hexadecimal escapes. These are errors in an application text format with no specified relay-facing input or response.

requirements.summary: Treat an invalid serialized namespace or track name as an error, with application-defined handling.
requirements.rationale: The draft expressly leaves the response to invalid textual names application-defined. Neither the local name parser nor a deterministic protocol error outcome is exposed to the relay-side harness.

requirements.summary: Do not change the payload bytes of an Object identified by its track namespace, track name, Group ID, and Object ID over time.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher originates the immutable bytes. The harness can compare repeated deliveries of the same object identity, allowing unavailability and separately mutable properties described in Sections 2.5 and 9.1.

requirements.summary: Preserve object payloads without combining, splitting, or otherwise modifying them.
requirements.rationale: This sentence explicitly constrains a relay's handling of an already-produced payload. The Original Publisher instead owns payload creation and is not performing the relay operation.

requirements.summary: Do not send Objects from two distinct Subgroups on the same stream when delivering a subscription.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publisher sends subscription streams under Section 5.1. Group and Subgroup identities in SUBGROUP_HEADER (Section 11.4.2) allow the harness to check stream isolation; this statement is not a FETCH-stream rule.

requirements.summary: Do not distribute one Subgroup's subscription Objects across multiple streams unless one was reset prematurely or upstream conditions forced out-of-order Object IDs.
requirements.rationale: A normal contribution-publisher subscription can be observed without either stated exception. Repeated subgroup headers on separate streams are not automatically violations when a premature reset or the specified upstream condition applies.

requirements.summary: Reuse a Subgroup ID in different Groups without establishing a relationship between those Subgroups.
requirements.rationale: Subgroup IDs are scoped to a Group, and the Original Publisher assigns them. Reuse can be observed in headers as an optional capability; choosing distinct IDs does not fail a mandatory requirement.

requirements.summary: Set FIRST_OBJECT when opening a new Subgroup so its stream identifies the first Object ever published in that Subgroup.
requirements.rationale: The test observes initial publication by the Original Publisher, with FIRST_OBJECT encoded as bit 0x40 in Section 11.4.2. This does not require the bit on a later stream that starts after the first published Object.

requirements.summary: Set FIRST_OBJECT when forwarding a Subgroup beginning with its first-ever published Object.
requirements.rationale: The second FIRST_OBJECT sentence governs relay forwarding, distinct from the preceding Original Publisher obligation. A contribution publisher does not forward a received subgroup in this role.

requirements.summary: Construct Groups that are independently useful as subscription join points.
requirements.rationale: The Original Publisher chooses the content grouped together. Whether content is useful without other Groups depends on the application and potentially encrypted payload, not a deterministic MOQT protocol observation.

requirements.summary: Avoid making Objects in one Group depend on Objects in other Groups.
requirements.rationale: Cross-Group content dependency is an application property of the Original Publisher's Objects. The protocol exposes Group IDs but not a complete dependency model from which a relay could decide this recommendation.

requirements.summary: Assign published Group IDs that increase with the internal media clock within each Track.
requirements.rationale: The relevant time is explicitly the media's internal clock, while descending delivery and network reordering are permitted. Relay arrival order alone cannot establish this media-semantic property for arbitrary payloads.

requirements.summary: Avoid FETCH or SUBSCRIBE range filters spanning multiple Groups when a Track's Group IDs do not increase with media time.
requirements.rationale: This advice is directed to subscribers choosing request filters for nonmonotonic Tracks. A contribution publisher responds to these requests and does not choose the subscriber's range.

requirements.summary: Encode at least one byte in every Track Namespace Field Value.
requirements.rationale: Publisher-originated track announcements expose namespace fields for inspection. The restriction is on each field, not on the number of fields; the empty namespace tuple remains allowed.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after receiving a Track Namespace Field Length of zero.
requirements.rationale: A relay acting as the subscriber can send a request containing an empty namespace field. The publishing endpoint's receive validation is required even though it primarily sends media.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a received namespace has more than 32 fields.
requirements.rationale: The limit applies to received Track Namespaces regardless of endpoint role. A 33-field request is a deterministic stimulus for the contribution publisher.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a received Track Namespace exceeds 4096 bytes.
requirements.rationale: Namespace size is the sum of its Field Length values, excluding their varint encodings. A namespace-bearing control message tests this limit independently of a Full Track Name.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a received Full Track Name exceeds 4096 bytes.
requirements.rationale: A Full Track Name adds the Track Name Length to the namespace field lengths. A request with a namespace within the limit but a combined total over it exercises the second condition of this MUST.

requirements.summary: Cancel corresponding subscriptions to the offending publisher after detecting a Malformed Track.
requirements.rationale: The detecting actor is the subscriber receiving malformed Objects; Section 3.3.2 defines request cancellation. Contribution-publisher testing does not turn that publisher into a receiving subscriber.

requirements.summary: Cancel corresponding fetches from the offending publisher after detecting a Malformed Track.
requirements.rationale: Fetch cancellation is independently actionable from subscription cancellation, but it remains a duty of the subscriber that detects malformed upstream data.

requirements.summary: Deliver an application error when detecting a Malformed Track.
requirements.rationale: The application notification belongs to the subscriber's malformed-track handling; it is not a contribution publisher response to a relay request.

requirements.summary: Immediately terminate downstream subscriptions with PUBLISH_DONE after detecting a Malformed Track.
requirements.rationale: This is the relay's downstream fan-out reaction to upstream malformed data. An Original Publisher does not receive an upstream track to relay.

requirements.summary: Immediately reset downstream fetch streams with MALFORMED_TRACK after detecting a Malformed Track.
requirements.rationale: Resetting fetch data streams is a separate relay action from terminating subscriptions. Its trigger is detection while relaying another publisher's Track, outside the contribution-publisher role.

requirements.summary: Do not cache Objects that trigger Malformed Track status.
requirements.rationale: The paragraph constrains a receiver's cache after detecting incoming malformed Objects. The contribution publisher's production or storage of its own Objects is not this receiving-cache operation.

requirements.summary: Use different Track Names and/or Track Namespaces for Tracks in the same MOQT scope containing different data at the same time.
requirements.rationale: The publisher chooses names for the Tracks it originates. Comparing their Full Track Names and supplied content in the same authority/path scope tests uniqueness without inventing a global namespace rule.

requirements.summary: Do not modify an unsupported Property, subject to the Mandatory Track Property handling exception.
requirements.rationale: The antecedent explicitly identifies a relay that does not support the Property. Original Publisher authoring of properties is distinct from preserving an unknown property while forwarding it.

requirements.summary: Forward unsupported Properties with their Track or Object unless the Mandatory Track Property rules apply.
requirements.rationale: This same-line MUST is the unknown-property forwarding duty of relays. Section 2.5.1 supplies the exception for tracks carrying unsupported mandatory extensions.

requirements.summary: Cache unsupported Properties with their Track or Object unless they are Mandatory Track Properties requiring special handling.
requirements.rationale: This obligation concerns preserving received unknown properties in a relay cache, not a contribution publisher's local source data. Section 9.1 allows relay caching to be optional; properties accompany any cached Track or Object.

requirements.summary: Replace cached unknown properties with the most recently received set, removing unknown values omitted from that set.
requirements.rationale: Replacement and removal describe one set-replacement operation in a receiving relay cache. A contribution publisher originates its property set rather than reconciling versions received from upstream.

requirements.summary: Do not merge sets of unknown properties received in different messages.
requirements.rationale: The rule forbids relay-side reconciliation that would invent an unknown-property set. It does not constrain an Original Publisher composing its own outgoing properties.

requirements.summary: Modify a supported Property when its definition permits modification.
requirements.rationale: This permission is conditioned on the relay understanding and obeying the property's processing definition. It is not a general grant to the contribution publisher under this occurrence.

requirements.summary: Add a supported Property when its definition permits addition.
requirements.rationale: Adding metadata at a relay is an independent allowed operation in the MAY list. The explicit relay actor excludes Original Publisher creation of properties from this record.

requirements.summary: Remove a supported Property when its definition permits removal.
requirements.rationale: Removal is separately permitted only under the understood property's rules. The contribution-publisher role does not perform this transformation of a received Track or Object.

requirements.summary: Cache a supported Property according to its definition's processing rules.
requirements.rationale: This clause allows a relay's property-specific caching choice; it is separate from modifying, adding, or removing the Property and lies outside publisher conformance.

requirements.summary: Use application-specific Property code points 0x38-0x3F or 0x3800-0x3FFF without registration.
requirements.rationale: The publisher application may emit these code points for its metadata, which the relay can observe as an optional capability. This record preserves Section 2.5's literal ranges; Section 15.8 inconsistently lists 0x78-0x7F for the one-byte reservation.

requirements.summary: Forward application-specific properties unchanged when the application format is not understood.
requirements.rationale: The actor is explicitly a relay lacking the application format, and the operation preserves another endpoint's metadata. The Original Publisher knows the context of the properties it creates.

requirements.summary: Do not interpret application-specific property semantics when the application format is not understood.
requirements.rationale: The prohibition prevents a relay from assigning meaning to code points that different applications may reuse differently. It does not prohibit a contribution publisher interpreting its own application metadata.

requirements.summary: Use Mandatory Track Property types 0x4000-0x7FFF only at Track scope.
requirements.rationale: This section defines a protocol placement constraint, with an Object carrying one expressly malformed. A publishing endpoint's Track and Object property fields are relay-visible, unlike the separate IANA registration requirement in Section 15.8.

requirements.summary: Do not process a Track received with an unsupported Mandatory Track Property in PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE_OK, or FETCH_OK.
requirements.rationale: Although the sentence says endpoint, its trigger is receiving Track Properties in messages addressed to the subscriber role. A contribution publisher sending those properties is not the receiver constrained here.

requirements.summary: Do not forward a Track received with an unsupported Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Forwarding is an independently forbidden action under the same MUST NOT, performed by a relay after it receives the Track as a subscriber. An Original Publisher does not forward an upstream Track.

requirements.summary: Reject PUBLISH with REQUEST_ERROR and UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION when it contains an unknown Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: The response is sent by the subscriber accepting or rejecting another endpoint's publication. It is the harness-side subscriber action, not the contribution publisher's required behavior.

requirements.summary: Cancel a subscription when SUBSCRIBE_OK contains an unsupported Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: The receiver of SUBSCRIBE_OK is the subscriber that requested the Track. Section 3.3.2 provides cancellation mechanics, but this occurrence imposes no action on an Original Publisher.

requirements.summary: Send pending downstream subscribers REQUEST_ERROR with UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION after receiving SUBSCRIBE_OK with an unknown Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: This conditional duty exists when a subscriber is also a relay with pending downstream requests. It requires an upstream subscription and downstream fan-out absent from the contribution-publisher role.

requirements.summary: Cancel a fetch when FETCH_OK contains an unsupported Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber received an extension it cannot process in the response to its FETCH. Cancellation under Section 3.3.2 is outside an endpoint acting only as the contribution publisher.

requirements.summary: Send the downstream fetch requester REQUEST_ERROR with UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION if no FETCH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR has yet been sent downstream.
requirements.rationale: The relay has learned of an unsupported Mandatory Track Property upstream and must reject its still-pending downstream fetch. This is distinct from the publisher's later SHOULD advice about known subscriber support.

requirements.summary: Reset a downstream fetch stream if data has already been forwarded before an unsupported Mandatory Track Property is detected.
requirements.rationale: This branch applies to a relay that has already begun forwarding fetched data. A contribution publisher does not discover an upstream mandatory extension while forwarding another publisher's fetch.

requirements.summary: Reject SUBSCRIBE with REQUEST_ERROR and UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION when the publisher knows the subscriber lacks a Mandatory Track Property required by the Track.
requirements.rationale: The harness can establish the subscriber's lack of support before requesting the Track and observe this recommended response. The test must establish publisher knowledge; mere absence of extension negotiation is not proof of that precondition.

requirements.summary: Reject FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR and UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION when the publisher knows the subscriber lacks a Mandatory Track Property required by the Track.
requirements.rationale: FETCH is a separate request path under the SHOULD lead-in. Once lack of support is known to the publisher, a relay-side request exposes the recommended error response independently of SUBSCRIBE handling.

requirements.summary: Do not initiate PUBLISH for a Track when the publisher knows the subscriber lacks a Mandatory Track Property required by that Track.
requirements.rationale: A controlled publication attempt with prior established knowledge of unsupported mandatory metadata can be observed for suppression of PUBLISH. The evaluator must bound the attempt and establish that knowledge rather than infer non-support from silence.

requirements.summary: Support and negotiate QUIC DATAGRAM on the QUIC connection used for MOQT.
requirements.rationale: The requirement applies to the transport of a publishing endpoint using native QUIC or WebTransport over HTTP/3; the handshake exposes DATAGRAM negotiation.

requirements.summary: Do not use a moqt URI whose authority has an empty host.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher acting as a client consumes a connection URI. An empty-host input can be supplied and failure to initiate a session observed; no particular diagnostic or session error code is mandated.

requirements.summary: Optionally use a locally processed fragment identifier with a moqt URI.
requirements.rationale: A publishing client may consume a URI fragment, but this paragraph explicitly keeps it off the wire and local to the client. The draft defines no registered fragment semantics with an externally checkable effect.

requirements.summary: Begin any moqt URI fragment with a registered type identifier, a colon, and the type-specific value.
requirements.rationale: This constrains a publisher client's local URI fragment syntax. Fragments are not transmitted and Section 15.3 initializes the type registry empty, so this draft supplies neither a usable registered fragment nor a protocol rejection oracle.

requirements.summary: Use only ASCII lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens in a URI fragment type identifier.
requirements.rationale: The permitted character set applies when a publishing client handles fragments, but fragments remain local and this draft specifies no externally visible handling of malformed fragment types.

requirements.summary: Choose native QUIC or WebTransport for a client session.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher can be the initiating client. Its chosen allowed transport is observable in session establishment; the permission does not require implementing both alternatives.

requirements.summary: Optionally associate one or more transport-specific connection URLs with a track.
requirements.rationale: A publishing application can maintain track connection URLs, but this paragraph defines no message that exposes that association to the peer; establishing a connection alone cannot prove the per-track mapping.

requirements.summary: Include every Setup Option required for the negotiated MOQT version in SETUP.
requirements.rationale: Both endpoint roles include publishing endpoints. For the checked-in version, Section 10.3.1 requires the native-QUIC client to carry URI authority and path in SETUP, which the peer can inspect. Optional options are not made mandatory by this rule.

requirements.summary: Specify the existing extensions usable with each new MOQT version.
requirements.rationale: This directs authors of future protocol versions to document extension compatibility; it is not behavior of a contribution publisher implementing draft 18.

requirements.summary: Specify the existing MOQT versions usable with a new extension.
requirements.rationale: The actor is the author of an extension specification, whose version-compatibility declaration cannot be an endpoint conformance action.

requirements.summary: Do not originate use of a namespace whose first tuple field starts with a period unless its meaning is IANA-registered.
requirements.rationale: Publishing a track or namespace uses its namespace and is covered by this restriction. The following receive rule permits passing an unrecognized reserved namespace to the application; it does not authorize originating an unregistered reserved namespace.

requirements.summary: Pass requests for unrecognized reserved namespaces to the application unless another rule specifies otherwise.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint receives track requests, but the mandated action is delivery across its internal application interface. No response or outcome is specified for the application, so a wire trace alone cannot establish this handoff.

requirements.summary: Do not use a namespace whose first tuple field is exactly a single period for any purpose.
requirements.rationale: The absolute reservation covers publisher-originated track and namespace operations, beyond merely treating the name as unknown. Trace inspection can detect prohibited use; explicit publication and incoming-request rules are separately anchored below.

requirements.summary: Do not publish tracks under a namespace whose first field is exactly a period.
requirements.rationale: This clause forbids track publication by any endpoint, including an original publisher. It is independently observable from namespace announcements.

requirements.summary: Do not publish namespaces whose first field is exactly a period.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is a separate operation from publishing a track, so its prohibition needs its own result even if track publication already rejects the name.

requirements.summary: Reject requests referencing a namespace whose first tuple field is exactly a period with DOES_NOT_EXIST.
requirements.rationale: A publisher receiving a request for this reserved namespace has a precise mandated negative response, independently of whether it ever originates such names.

requirements.summary: Do not publish application tracks whose namespace first field is .session.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publishing application is constrained here, while transport-managed extension tracks are permitted in this namespace. Supplying an application track checks the prohibited path without forbidding future transport extensions.

requirements.summary: Do not publish application namespaces whose first field is .session.
requirements.rationale: The namespace publication API can fail this rule independently of application track publication; wire inspection checks that the attempted application namespace is not advertised.

requirements.summary: Do not forward requests for session-level tracks or namespaces to other sessions.
requirements.rationale: This prohibits cross-session forwarding by relays; an original contribution publisher does not forward requests between sessions.

requirements.summary: Reject requests with first namespace field .session and an empty Track Name with DOES_NOT_EXIST.
requirements.rationale: The explicitly nonexistent empty session track has a mandated error for a receiving publisher even if session-level extensions are otherwise supported.

requirements.summary: Reject requests for unrecognized session-level tracks or namespaces with REQUEST_ERROR carrying DOES_NOT_EXIST instead of passing them to the application.
requirements.rationale: This is the .session exception to the general reserved-namespace handoff rule. A publisher's protocol rejection is observable; an instrumented application is not required to establish the specified wire outcome.

requirements.summary: Begin bidirectional request streams only with one of the seven listed request types or a negotiated additional type.
requirements.rationale: A publisher opens PUBLISH and PUBLISH_NAMESPACE request streams; inspecting each initial message checks this endpoint-wide prohibition while allowing negotiated extensions.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a bidirectional stream begins with an unpermitted message type.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint accepts peer request streams and must enforce the same initial-type rule; a deliberately invalid initial message gives an exact session-error oracle.

requirements.summary: Buffer early unidirectional Object data until both control streams arrive and setup is complete.
requirements.rationale: The Object-receiving branch of this recommendation is a subscriber duty. A contribution publisher sends Objects rather than receiving subscribed data.

requirements.summary: Buffer early bidirectional request data until both control streams arrive and setup is complete.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint can receive SUBSCRIBE before SETUP. Delaying SETUP and then completing it exposes whether the early request was retained and handled; the following MAY separately permits declining buffering and resetting the request.

requirements.summary: Optionally reset early bidirectional requests before session establishment when buffering is unwanted or the message type unsupported.
requirements.rationale: The publishing endpoint may decline an early request through a visible stream reset. Exercising this permission is conditional on its buffering policy and is not a mandate to reset every early stream.

requirements.summary: Keep the control stream open at the transport layer throughout the session lifetime.
requirements.rationale: Ending a publisher request does not authorize ending its session control stream. Stream FIN and reset events can be checked against the still-active session lifetime.

requirements.summary: Avoid parameters requiring negotiation before receiving peer SETUP unless the application requires the extension or peer support is known.
requirements.rationale: Publisher messages can be pipelined during setup. A controlled configuration excluding the two stated exceptions allows inspection of their parameters before the peer's SETUP arrives.

requirements.summary: Optionally defer upstream subscriptions until handshake completion or reject 0-RTT to mitigate replay resource exhaustion.
requirements.rationale: These alternative mitigations address relays creating upstream work from replayed downstream requests, not the original publisher's contribution session.

requirements.summary: Allow either endpoint to cancel a request after its request stream opens.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher originates requests and can also receive them; the cancellation permission applies in either role. Its effect can be observed by cancelling an opened publication request.

requirements.summary: Cancel a request by resetting any still-open sending direction of its request stream.
requirements.rationale: A bidirectional request has independently open send and receive directions. Resetting the publisher's send direction is separately observable from asking the peer to stop sending.

requirements.summary: Cancel a request by sending STOP_SENDING for any still-open receiving direction of its request stream.
requirements.rationale: The receive direction remains open even if the endpoint resets its send direction. STOP_SENDING supplies an independent transport observation for the cancellation recommendation.

requirements.summary: Send REQUEST_ERROR when rejecting a request without application processing.
requirements.rationale: A publisher can reject a request at the protocol layer before application work. The recommendation specifies a wire response independently of closing the response stream.

requirements.summary: FIN the request stream when rejecting a request without application processing.
requirements.rationale: Sending an error does not itself close the publisher's response direction; its FIN is an independently checkable second action under the same SHOULD.

requirements.summary: Use a relevant Section 3.3.3 error code when resetting or sending STOP_SENDING on a request stream.
requirements.rationale: A publisher application's cancellation reason can be controlled. In an ordinary cancellation the CANCELLED code expresses that reason on either transport cancellation operation.

requirements.summary: Use a relevant stream error code when resetting or sending STOP_SENDING on any stream.
requirements.rationale: This recommendation includes publisher data streams in addition to request streams. A controlled voluntary subgroup cancellation exposes the choice of the CANCELLED code.

requirements.summary: Close the session when receiving an unknown unidirectional stream type.
requirements.rationale: Every publisher receives the peer's unidirectional control stream and must validate stream types. This sentence requires closure but does not name a specific error code, unlike the invalid request-stream rule.

requirements.summary: Optionally use any error message when terminating a session.
requirements.rationale: A publisher application can choose the free-form termination message; the peer can observe the selected reason. This permission imposes no fixed wording or requirement to provide a nonempty message.

requirements.summary: Use a relevant session error code when terminating the session.
requirements.rationale: The publisher selects a session termination code. A controlled normal shutdown has the explicitly defined NO_ERROR code and avoids guessing which internal error caused an arbitrary closure.

requirements.summary: Optionally send STOP_SENDING or terminate the subscription after timing out waiting for a new object header on an open subgroup stream.
requirements.rationale: The endpoint in this conditional is waiting for incoming Object data and therefore acts as a subscriber. A contribution publisher supplies those headers rather than timing out while receiving them.

requirements.summary: Optionally escalate a request-specific or subscription-specific error into a session error.
requirements.rationale: This permission applies to a publisher handling a faulty request and can be exercised under a configured escalation policy. Observing session closure demonstrates the option, without requiring escalation or a particular code for all request failures.

requirements.summary: After sending GOAWAY, close with GOAWAY_TIMEOUT when its indicated timeout expires and subscriptions or fetches remain open.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint can send GOAWAY while serving subscriptions. Keeping one open past a nonzero advertised timeout provides the condition for checking the recommended close code and timing.

requirements.summary: A server with upstream subscriptions should send GOAWAY downstream before unsubscribing upstream.
requirements.rationale: The described server is a subscriber upstream and has downstream subscribers, hence performs relay migration. An original contribution publisher has no upstream subscription to drain.

requirements.summary: After receiving GOAWAY, wait for Established subscriptions to end before closing the session with NO_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher can be the client while publishing on Established subscriptions. The recommendation covers its orderly drain; the later text permits further delay for expected Objects, so no immediate-close deadline is inferred.

requirements.summary: A non-relay endpoint may implement only the protocol functionality needed for its tasks.
requirements.rationale: An original publisher is a non-relay endpoint and can choose a reduced implementation. A black-box rejection does not establish which functionality is implemented versus disabled by policy, and the supported subset is not prescribed here.

requirements.summary: Respond to unsupported messages with the appropriate NOT_SUPPORTED error rather than ignoring them.
requirements.rationale: The limited publisher's declared unsupported but protocol-defined request can be sent and its response checked. This does not override separate fatal rules for unknown stream types or malformed messages.

requirements.summary: Implement every MOQT message defined by this draft when acting as a relay.
requirements.rationale: Full message coverage is expressly required of relays; the preceding permission lets non-relay contribution publishers implement a subset.

requirements.summary: Implement the relay processing rules of Section 9.
requirements.rationale: Implementing message formats alone does not fulfill the separate Section 9 relay-processing duty. Both apply to relays and are outside the contribution publisher role.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one SUBSCRIBE_OK or REQUEST_ERROR for each SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.rationale: This is the publisher's explicit acceptance-or-rejection cardinality rule. Recording the full request response catches both missing responses and duplicated or contradictory responses.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one PUBLISH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR for each PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber sends this response to a publisher-initiated subscription. The contribution publisher receives it; its reaction to duplicates is a separate recommendation.

requirements.summary: Close the session with a protocol error if the peer sends more than one subscription response.
requirements.rationale: For the publisher role, the peer's responses are PUBLISH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR. Two responses for the same PUBLISH exercise the publisher's receiving duty rather than the subscriber's response cardinality duty.

requirements.summary: Save as the Joining Location the Largest Location communicated when SUBSCRIBE_OK, PUBLISH, or REQUEST_UPDATE_OK changes Forward State from 0 to 1.
requirements.rationale: Although retaining the value is internal, Section 10.12.2.1 requires a Joining FETCH to end at that saved location. Advancing the track after enabling forwarding distinguishes retained Joining Location from the current Largest Object through fetched Objects.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH without knowing the client is interested in and authorized for the content.
requirements.rationale: This sentence restricts unsolicited relay forwarding, not the original publisher's ability to initiate subscriptions after SETUP. The interest and authorization conditions are conjunctive prerequisites for the same relay action.

requirements.summary: Optionally subscribe to a track that the same endpoint is publishing.
requirements.rationale: The permitted action is initiating a subscription and receiving looped-back Objects in the subscriber role. Being the same endpoint's publisher does not turn its optional self-subscription into a contribution publisher duty; only relays must serve it.

requirements.summary: Fail a request that would establish a second same-role subscription to a track with DUPLICATE_SUBSCRIPTION.
requirements.rationale: The same-role uniqueness rule includes the publisher role. A second SUBSCRIBE for a track already served in the session must fail, without forbidding a distinct opposite-role subscription.

requirements.summary: Reject SUBSCRIBE with DUPLICATE_SUBSCRIPTION when the track already has a Pending publisher-initiated subscription.
requirements.rationale: This specifies the crossed-initiation race for the publisher. Delaying PUBLISH_OK and sending SUBSCRIBE for the same track exposes the Pending-state rejection independently of the Established-state duplicate rule.

requirements.summary: Terminate a Pending subscriber-initiated subscription before sending PUBLISH_OK for a crossed PUBLISH on the same track.
requirements.rationale: This resolves the other side of crossed subscription initiation: the subscriber abandons its own SUBSCRIBE before accepting the publisher's PUBLISH. It does not describe publisher state transitions.

requirements.summary: Begin sending available incomplete Objects to avoid additional latency.
requirements.rationale: An original publisher can receive a payload incrementally from its application. Holding the final chunk while observing a writable subgroup stream distinguishes incremental transmission from waiting for object completion.

requirements.summary: Optionally send Objects for a PUBLISH-initiated subscription before receiving PUBLISH_OK.
requirements.rationale: A peer can delay its response and observe permitted early delivery. The paragraph acknowledges later rejection or Forward=0, so early Objects alone are not evidence of violating a response-dependent forwarding decision.

requirements.summary: Reset every open stream associated with SUBSCRIBE after receiving request STOP_SENDING.
requirements.rationale: The publisher may discard subscription state on cancellation, but must reset its still-open associated streams. Multiple open subgroups ensure cancellation is checked across the subscription rather than on only one stream.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH_DONE until all related Object streams have been closed.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's closure ordering is observable at its transport event boundary. Section 10.11 explains that the bidi request stream carries PUBLISH_DONE and closes after it, so related streams here cannot mean that same response stream.

requirements.summary: Do not send Objects for a subscription request that ends with REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: This is the subscription error path: rejecting a SUBSCRIBE does not establish an Object delivery right. It is not generalized to FETCH, whose Section 5.2 explicitly allows cached Objects before a later error, or used to outlaw the pre-response PUBLISH permission in Section 5.1.

requirements.summary: Optionally specify an AbsoluteStart location below the publisher's Largest Object.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber selects the filter start; this permission defines a valid subscriber input rather than requiring a publisher to retrieve historical Objects. The publisher's rejection and range-delivery duties are separately stated below.

requirements.summary: Optionally specify an AbsoluteRange start below the publisher's Largest Object.
requirements.rationale: This authorizes the subscriber's choice of range start, including a past location. It does not oblige the publisher to retain unavailable history or waive the separately specified invalid-range response.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if Start Group plus End Group Delta exceeds 2^64 minus one.
requirements.rationale: A publisher decodes subscription filters from its subscriber. Individually encodable values whose sum overflows the allowed Group ID expose the required receive-side session failure.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION upon receiving an undefined Subscription Filter type.
requirements.rationale: The publishing endpoint parses the subscriber's filter; a type outside 0x1 through 0x4 has a precise error outcome, unlike an otherwise valid filter that the publisher cannot satisfy.

requirements.summary: Reject an unsatisfiable subscription filter or one whose entire End Group is already published with REQUEST_ERROR code INVALID_RANGE.
requirements.rationale: Both stated conditions lead to the same recommended request error. A controlled publishing history makes completed End Groups known and distinguishes this request-level rejection from malformed-filter session closure.

requirements.summary: Do not send subscription Objects outside the requested filter range.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's outgoing Object Locations are compared with the accepted Start Location and inclusive End Group. Objects below the start or in groups beyond the end remain prohibited even if available at the publisher.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one FETCH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to each FETCH.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher receiving FETCH must send a single acceptance or error response. Counting these response types independently of the data stream catches missing and duplicated responses.

requirements.summary: Optionally send STOP_SENDING on an already-open FETCH data stream when cancelling the FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The fetch requester may additionally cancel its receiving data stream. This is a subscriber action and does not replace its mandatory cancellation of the bidi request stream.

requirements.summary: Send STOP_SENDING on the bidirectional request stream when cancelling FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber must signal cancellation on the FETCH request itself even when it also stops the data stream. The publisher's required reaction is the next independently anchored obligation.

requirements.summary: Reset the FETCH bidirectional request stream after receiving STOP_SENDING cancellation.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's request-stream reset can be observed separately from the associated data reset. The incoming STOP_SENDING on the FETCH request establishes the cancellation trigger.

requirements.summary: Reset the associated FETCH unidirectional data stream after receiving STOP_SENDING cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Resetting only the bidi request leaves the fetch payload stream active. Opening that data stream before cancellation makes the second mandatory transport action independently observable.

requirements.summary: Send a single REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: An original publisher can receive namespace discovery requests. Their response cardinality is independently checkable from both response ordering and the separate SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS path.

requirements.summary: Make REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR the first response message on the SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE bidirectional stream.
requirements.rationale: A publisher could send exactly one response yet wrongly precede it with NAMESPACE. This ordering clause therefore requires a separate observable result.

requirements.summary: Send a single REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.
requirements.rationale: Track discovery uses a distinct request and response path from namespace discovery. A publisher must preserve the single-response rule for this request type as well.

requirements.summary: Make REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR the first response message on the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS bidirectional stream.
requirements.rationale: A stream-credit-constrained publisher can emit PUBLISH_BLOCKED on this response stream, but the required acceptance or error must be first. This does not require PUBLISH on another stream to arrive in any order.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH for a track after sending PUBLISH_BLOCKED for it.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_BLOCKED lets the subscriber initiate SUBSCRIBE instead. Restoring credit while the discovery request remains active tests that the publisher does not later initiate the forbidden PUBLISH for that track.

requirements.summary: After track-discovery cancellation, do not send further relay PUBLISH messages without known client interest and authorization.
requirements.rationale: The paragraph expressly permits original publishers to continue PUBLISH after SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS cancellation; only relays retain this interest-and-authorization restriction.

requirements.summary: Optionally send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to any subscriber to announce available tracks in a namespace.
requirements.rationale: An original publisher can advertise its namespace without waiting for a discovery subscription. The observable announcement demonstrates the permission without making announcements necessary for all publishing.

requirements.summary: Optionally SUBSCRIBE or FETCH tracks without first receiving their PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: This removes a namespace-announcement prerequisite for the subscriber's choice of requests; it is not an instruction for a contribution publisher to originate subscriptions or fetches.

requirements.summary: When authoritative for a namespace, send NAMESPACE to each subscriber whose SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE matches the namespace or a prefix.
requirements.rationale: The authoritative-publisher branch directly applies to the contribution source. Exact and proper-prefix subscriptions expose its obligation to report the namespace on matching discovery streams.

requirements.summary: After authorized upstream PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, send NAMESPACE to subscribers with matching namespace discovery prefixes.
requirements.rationale: The second conditional branch is a relay forwarding knowledge received from an upstream publisher. It is separated from the authoritative-source branch because it has a different actor and contribution applicability.

requirements.summary: Optionally send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to other subscribers without a matching SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: This explicitly permits the publisher's announcement to subscribers outside the mandatory NAMESPACE discovery-recipient set; it uses PUBLISH_NAMESPACE rather than the discovery response message.

requirements.summary: Report received namespace publication REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR to the application.
requirements.rationale: A publisher receives these results, but the specified handoff informs an internal application decision and mandates no subsequent protocol action. A wire response alone cannot prove notification occurred.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber accepts or rejects the publisher's namespace announcement. Response cardinality belongs to that receiving subscriber, while the publisher has a separate duplicate-response reaction.

requirements.summary: Make REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR the first response message on a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE bidi stream.
requirements.rationale: The same subscriber response also has an independently enforceable first-message constraint. The contribution publisher does not send that response, so this clause remains outside its actor scope.

requirements.summary: Close the session with a protocol error if more than one response is received for PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: The peer can send two REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR messages on the publisher's namespace request stream; the publishing endpoint's recommended session closure is directly visible.

requirements.summary: Avoid using PUBLISH_NAMESPACE as a path-discovery mechanism through richly connected relay networks.
requirements.rationale: This cautions against a relay-network routing design because namespace publication provides no loop protection. It does not restrict an original publisher's ordinary namespace announcement to a subscriber.

requirements.summary: Optionally send SUBSCRIBE or FETCH for a track to any publisher.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses the source to request; this permission neither directs a contribution publisher to send requests nor mandates acceptance of every incoming request.

requirements.summary: When an accepted PUBLISH_NAMESPACE exactly matches a track namespace, request that track only from senders of those announcements.
requirements.rationale: The recommendation narrows the subscriber's source selection after namespace discovery. The contribution publisher advertises a namespace but does not choose upstream track sources.

requirements.summary: Make a best effort to apply Subscriber Priority updates to every Object not yet scheduled.
requirements.rationale: The recommendation constrains internal scheduling state. The draft leaves already-scheduled handling and the scheduling boundary implementation-dependent, so wire order cannot establish which Objects were eligible when the update arrived or whether best effort was made.

requirements.summary: Among schedulable Objects with different Subscriber Priorities, select the Object with the highest Subscriber Priority first.
requirements.rationale: This is the first publisher scheduling criterion and uses the lower numerical priority. Lines 2413-2418 make the scheduling boundary depend on the transport interface, so peer arrival order is not a mandatory oracle for internal Object selection.

requirements.summary: For equal Subscriber Priority, select the schedulable Object with the highest Publisher Priority first.
requirements.rationale: The second comparator is independently meaningful once Subscriber Priority ties. The draft allows internal serialization order or transport packet scheduling to realize it, and does not guarantee externally received Object order.

requirements.summary: For tied Subscriber and Publisher Priorities in the same request and track, use Group Order to select between different groups.
requirements.rationale: This tie-breaker is limited to one request and track and controls the publisher's internal scheduling selection. Cross-stream delivery order need not preserve that selection, as the section explicitly leaves its transport realization implementation-dependent.

requirements.summary: For tied priorities within the same request, track, and group, select the lowest Subgroup ID first when both Objects use Subgroup forwarding.
requirements.rationale: Subgroup ID is the last specified comparator for stream-forwarded Objects. It is separated from the datagram Object-ID comparator, but actual scheduling remains internal and mixed forwarding preferences have no prescribed order.

requirements.summary: For tied priorities within the same request, track, and group, select the lowest Object ID first when both Objects use Datagram forwarding.
requirements.rationale: The datagram branch compares Object IDs instead of Subgroup IDs and can fail independently of stream ordering. Scheduling realization is explicitly implementation-dependent, and datagram arrival order cannot establish the internal comparator.

requirements.summary: Prioritize control streams above bidirectional request streams.
requirements.rationale: A publisher maintains both control and request streams, but their priority relationship is an internal transport scheduling choice. The section's implementation-dependent scheduling boundary prevents inferring it solely from the peer's arrival order.

requirements.summary: Prioritize bidirectional request streams above subscribed Object delivery.
requirements.rationale: Request-versus-Object priority is a separate ordering edge from control-versus-request priority. Both involve internal publisher scheduling and neither specifies a guaranteed wire arrival sequence.

requirements.summary: Optionally prioritize bidirectional request streams relative to one another by their specified Subscriber Priority.
requirements.rationale: Publishers send responses on request streams and may schedule those streams by the subscriber's value. The optional internal scheduling policy has no mandated observable ordering under the implementation-dependent scheduling definition.

requirements.summary: Respect Subscriber Priority on downstream relay subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: This addresses a relay reconciling downstream subscriptions, not an original publisher assigning or honoring priorities directly under Section 7.2.

requirements.summary: Respect the original publisher's priorities on downstream relay subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: Preserving the original publisher's priority intent is independent of honoring downstream Subscriber Priority, but the actor for both clauses is explicitly the relay.

requirements.summary: Avoid directly copying incoming Subscriber Priority into upstream relay subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: The recommendation concerns aggregating potentially conflicting downstream interests into an upstream request. An original contribution publisher has no such relay subscription mapping.

requirements.summary: Avoid directly copying incoming Group Order into upstream relay subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: Upstream Group Order selection can violate this advice independently of Subscriber Priority handling. It remains a relay-specific reconciliation policy rather than original publishing behavior.

requirements.summary: If a default priority exists, choose a value in the middle of the range, such as 128, to leave room for higher and lower priorities.
requirements.rationale: A publisher's default effective priority can be visible, but this recommendation supplies no precise boundary for the middle of the range. The value 128 is only an example, not a mandatory value; an automated acceptance threshold would add a constraint absent from this draft.

requirements.summary: When Object Delivery Timeout is nonzero, retain each Object's first-payload-byte time from upstream receipt or original application provision.
requirements.rationale: For an original publisher the clock starts when its application provides the first payload byte, not when transmission starts. Retention of that timestamp is internal state; expiry actions have their own separate externally testable obligations.

requirements.summary: With nonzero Object Delivery Timeout, check a subgroup Object's elapsed first-byte age before passing it to the transport for transmission.
requirements.rationale: The required check occurs at the publisher's internal transport handoff, which a peer cannot directly observe. An expired stream reset tests the following consequence but does not prove every pre-handoff age check happened.

requirements.summary: Reset the subgroup stream with DELIVERY_TIMEOUT when an Object's first-byte age exceeds Object Delivery Timeout before transport handoff.
requirements.rationale: Provide a timed Object while its existing subgroup stream is blocked, then release capacity after expiry. The publisher's reset and DELIVERY_TIMEOUT code are observable; bytes already buffered in the transport are outside this pre-handoff check.

requirements.summary: After an Object Delivery Timeout resets a subgroup stream, avoid opening another stream for further Objects in that subgroup.
requirements.rationale: The publisher controls future streams for the same group and subgroup. Supplying further Objects after the timeout allows a trace to reveal whether it opens a replacement stream despite the recommendation.

requirements.summary: Check Object Delivery Timeout before retransmitting Object data when the transport implementation permits it.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher retransmits through its transport, but the recommendation depends on whether that transport exposes a retransmission-time hook. A peer trace cannot establish that capability or the internal timeout check.

requirements.summary: Minimize data buffered in the underlying transport so expired subgroup data is not transmitted from untimed buffers.
requirements.rationale: This recommendation concerns internal transport queue size and supplies no quantitative buffering bound. Observing delayed data does not identify the layer that buffered it or prove failure to minimize the queue.

requirements.summary: Drop an Object datagram when its first-payload-byte age exceeds the nonzero Object Delivery Timeout.
requirements.rationale: The age that triggers the drop runs from the instant the original publisher application provided the first payload byte (draft lines 2485-2488 and 2505-2506), an event internal to the publisher. An Object datagram carries no production time, and a datagram the publisher dropped for age cannot be told apart at the protocol boundary from one lost or delayed on the path or never produced; a cooperating publisher cannot make that clock visible on the wire either. Unlike the subgroup rule (lines 2494-2496) the datagram rule has no reset or other wire action to observe.

requirements.summary: Minimize datagram queuing or use a datagram queue that supports time bounds.
requirements.rationale: These are alternative internal queue-management strategies, not two simultaneous duties. The draft sets neither a queue-size threshold nor an externally queryable mechanism, so packet timing alone cannot identify compliance with this advice.

requirements.summary: For Subgroup forwarding with a nonzero Subgroup Delivery Timeout, start its duration timer when all Objects are known to have been published.
requirements.rationale: An original publisher learns subgroup completion from its application, whereas a relay can learn it from upstream FIN. Starting and retaining this timer is internal; its expiry-triggered reset is a distinct externally observable obligation.

requirements.summary: Reset a subgroup stream if its Subgroup Delivery Timeout timer expires before all stream data is committed.
requirements.rationale: Signal application completion while withholding delivery acknowledgements past a nonzero subgroup deadline. The stream reset is visible even if all bytes and FIN were already sent; this occurrence does not itself mandate a particular reset code.

requirements.summary: Optionally terminate a subscription with PUBLISH_DONE code TOO_FAR_BEHIND when slow consumption causes resource limits to be exceeded.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher can enforce configured resource limits even when delivery timeouts are disabled. Induced subscriber backpressure exercises this permitted termination without requiring the policy or inventing a universal queue limit.

requirements.summary: Optionally cache received Objects.
requirements.rationale: This permits a relay cache; it imposes no caching requirement on the original contribution publisher.

requirements.summary: Ignore subsequently received Objects with the same Full Track Name, Group ID and Object ID.
requirements.rationale: The optional duplicate-discard policy belongs to the caching relay receiving Objects from publishers, not the publisher producing them.

requirements.summary: Use duplicate Objects to update cached existence state or Object Properties only within the listed constraints.
requirements.rationale: This relay permission is limited to existing-to-nonexistent transitions and property-specific changes; it does not permit altering immutable publisher payloads.

requirements.summary: Treat a Track as Malformed when duplicate Objects differ in Forwarding Preference, Subgroup ID, Priority or Payload.
requirements.rationale: Although phrased as an endpoint duty, the trigger is receiving duplicate media Objects. It constrains the subscriber or receiving relay role described in Section 2.4.2, not the contribution publishing role.

requirements.summary: Change the representation of nonexistent Object ranges to a semantically equivalent representation.
requirements.rationale: The End-of-Group and redundant FETCH gap examples delimit a relay representation permission; they do not prescribe a publisher encoding choice.

requirements.summary: Do not cache an Object received after its nonexistence was already recorded.
requirements.rationale: Section 2.1 permits this arrival order without making the Track malformed. This clause advises the receiving caching relay, not the original publisher.

requirements.summary: Do not forward an Object received after its nonexistence was already recorded.
requirements.rationale: Suppressing onward delivery is independently observable from cache insertion, but both duties in this sentence belong to a caching relay.

requirements.summary: Store all Object fields defined in Section 11.2.1 except Object Properties whose definitions allow otherwise.
requirements.rationale: This specifies the content of a relay cache, including canonical header fields and payload. It does not require the contribution publisher to implement a receiving cache.

requirements.summary: Set Forward to 1 on a new upstream subscription regardless of the downstream Forward value.
requirements.rationale: The publisher observes this upstream SUBSCRIBE, but the recommendation governs the relay sending it. The explanation that publishers might deprioritize or reject Forward=0 requests is not an additional normative publisher obligation.

requirements.summary: Handle Objects for the same Track received from multiple publishers.
requirements.rationale: This is the relay's multi-source input obligation. The preceding paragraph allows resource-based rejection of additional publishers; it does not require an original publisher to accept competing publishers.

requirements.summary: Forward Objects from the Track's multiple publishers to matching Established subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: This is the downstream half of the relay's multiple-publisher interaction; it is separate from handling incoming Objects and does not constrain the original publisher's output logic.

requirements.summary: Attempt to deduplicate Objects before forwarding, subject to implementation constraints.
requirements.rationale: Deduplicating multiple publishers' Objects is a relay responsibility and is qualified by implementation constraints; it is not a publisher promise that duplicates never reach subscribers.

requirements.summary: Ensure subscribers are authorized to access content associated with the requested Track.
requirements.rationale: This section assigns access enforcement to the relay and leaves its policy outside the specification. It does not transfer that duty to an original publisher merely because the relay requests its Track.

requirements.summary: Establish an upstream subscription before sending downstream SUBSCRIBE_OK.
requirements.rationale: The ordering joins two relay sessions; the original publisher supplies the upstream response but is not responsible for when the relay acknowledges its downstream subscriber.

requirements.summary: Withhold FETCH_OK until sufficient information is available to send it.
requirements.rationale: The trigger is a relay lacking information for a downstream FETCH response. This specific occurrence does not state a generic publisher FETCH obligation.

requirements.summary: Follow Section 10.2.11 constraints on LARGEST_OBJECT.
requirements.rationale: This relay cross-reference requires the largest upstream-advertised or received Location. Section 10.2.11 separately states the publisher inclusion duty; that separate occurrence is cataloged as applicable.

requirements.summary: Do not reorder Objects received on a multi-object stream when forwarding unless application-specific information permits it.
requirements.rationale: The prohibition concerns preservation of an incoming stream by an intermediary; an original publisher is not forwarding a received multi-object stream.

requirements.summary: Do not drop Objects received on a multi-object stream when forwarding unless application-specific information permits it.
requirements.rationale: Dropping and reordering are independent relay behaviors. The exception is retained and this clause does not override the separate publisher timeout rules in Section 8.

requirements.summary: Aggregate authorized downstream subscriptions for the same Track into one upstream subscription.
requirements.rationale: Aggregation and sharing cached upstream content are optional relay behaviors. The Largest Object filter discussion advises the relay and does not require publisher-side aggregation.

requirements.summary: Perform graceful relay switchover by establishing replacement subscriptions before cancelling old ones.
requirements.rationale: The optional GOAWAY or network-switch procedure explicitly belongs to a subscriber. Publisher switchover is separately specified in Section 9.5.1.

requirements.summary: Reply to PUBLISH with PUBLISH_OK and Forward State=0 until subscribers are known for the new Track.
requirements.rationale: This is an optional relay response to a publisher. The publisher's obligation to honor Forward State follows Section 5.1; this permission does not change the actor to publisher.

requirements.summary: Verify publisher authorization for Tracks matching a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE namespace.
requirements.rationale: This branch concerns relay validation of namespace publication. The publisher is the subject of authorization, not the endpoint charged with enforcing it here.

requirements.summary: Verify publisher authorization for the Full Track Name in PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: Single-Track publication has its own authorization check at the relay, independently of PUBLISH_NAMESPACE acceptance. Neither check is a contribution-publisher enforcement duty.

requirements.summary: Do not infer authorization to publish other Tracks from authorization for one Track.
requirements.rationale: The wrapped MUST NOT constrains relay authorization scope; it does not require the original publisher to enforce permissions on other publishers.

requirements.summary: Do not infer authorization to publish Track Namespaces from authorization for one Track.
requirements.rationale: Namespace authorization is a separate scope from an individual Track grant. The receiver enforcing that separation is explicitly the relay.

requirements.summary: Send an explicit PUBLISH_NAMESPACE when requesting that subscriptions in a namespace be routed to this publisher.
requirements.rationale: Unlike adjacent relay authorization rules, this conditional duty names the publisher. With namespace routing requested by the application, the peer can observe the explicit namespace publication; a PUBLISH for one Track is insufficient.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBE to every publisher matching an Established Full Track Name subscription or a published namespace prefix.
requirements.rationale: Both matching paths govern relay upstream fanout. A publisher can receive the resulting SUBSCRIBE but cannot enforce distribution to other publishers.

requirements.summary: Forward PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to all matching subscribers.
requirements.rationale: This clause assigns namespace publication fanout to a relay. Its PUBLISH_NAMESPACE wording is preserved even though Section 10.18 describes NAMESPACE on namespace-subscription response streams.

requirements.summary: Forward PUBLISH to all matching subscribers.
requirements.rationale: Track publication fanout is the relay's downstream action. Section 9.5 later excludes forwarding PUBLISH to a subscriber with a held SUBSCRIBE for that Track.

requirements.summary: Choose any available matching publisher for an upstream FETCH when more than one exists.
requirements.rationale: Unlike SUBSCRIBE fanout, a relay may select one FETCH source. The original publisher's FETCH responder behavior does not include that source-selection choice.

requirements.summary: Reply SUBSCRIBE_OK to an authorized downstream SUBSCRIBE when at least one upstream subscription is Established.
requirements.rationale: The relay combines downstream authorization with upstream state; the contribution publisher does not hold this two-sided relay state.

requirements.summary: Send REQUEST_UPDATE with Forward=1 to all publishers when a Forward=1 downstream SUBSCRIBE meets upstream subscriptions in Forward State=0.
requirements.rationale: The update is observable at publishers, but the condition and all-publisher fanout are obligations of the relay. Publisher processing of a received update is specified separately in Sections 5.1 and 10.9.

requirements.summary: When no upstream subscription is Established, send SUBSCRIBE to every publisher of the requested namespace or its prefix.
requirements.rationale: Resolving a downstream request across known namespace publishers is relay routing. The publisher receives a request but does not select its peer's other upstream sessions.

requirements.summary: Use Forward=1 in the upstream SUBSCRIBE when the downstream SUBSCRIBE has Forward=1.
requirements.rationale: This mandatory propagation for Forward=1 is narrower than Section 9.2's recommendation to request Forward=1 generally. Both constrain the relay creating the request, not its publishing recipient.

requirements.summary: On incoming PUBLISH, send PUBLISH to each matching SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS subscriber except one already waiting on a held SUBSCRIBE for that Track.
requirements.rationale: This relay fanout requirement is qualified by the following held-subscription exception. It does not require a contribution publisher to receive and forward another publisher's PUBLISH.

requirements.summary: Proceed with a held downstream SUBSCRIBE when an incoming PUBLISH supplies its missing Track publisher.
requirements.rationale: The relay owns rendezvous state under Section 10.2.6 and resumes that request on publisher arrival; the arriving publisher does not own the held downstream request.

requirements.summary: Do not also forward PUBLISH to the subscriber whose held SUBSCRIBE is being satisfied.
requirements.rationale: This prevents duplicate downstream establishment by the relay in the held-SUBSCRIBE case; it is not a prohibition on the original publisher's initiating PUBLISH.

requirements.summary: After authorized PUBLISH_NAMESPACE matches existing subscriptions on other upstream sessions, send the new publisher SUBSCRIBE for each matching subscription.
requirements.rationale: Adding a new source to relay subscriptions is a relay multiple-publisher duty. Receiving those subscriptions is a possible publisher interaction, not responsibility for the fanout.

requirements.summary: Reply PUBLISH_OK to an authorized PUBLISH for a Track with Established downstream subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: The relay is the receiver and responder to this PUBLISH; the contribution publisher is the requester and cannot be assessed as the response sender.

requirements.summary: Use Forward State=1 in PUBLISH_OK when any downstream subscriber for the Track has Forward State=1.
requirements.rationale: A publisher observes the PUBLISH_OK field, but computing it from downstream demand is explicitly the relay's duty. Publisher Forward behavior remains governed by Section 5.1.

requirements.summary: Do not propagate an unknown or invalid control message that caused its Session to close into another Session.
requirements.rationale: This isolates control-message failures across relay sessions; it does not authorize or require the original publisher to forward control messages.

requirements.summary: Do not propagate an unknown or invalid Object that caused its Session to close into another Session.
requirements.rationale: The media-object branch independently isolates downstream relay sessions from an upstream error. The original publisher is not this intermediary.

requirements.summary: Gracefully switch relays by beginning publication on a new Session while continuing Objects on the old Session until subscriptions migrate.
requirements.rationale: A two-peer scenario can observe new-session PUBLISH_NAMESPACE or PUBLISH and overlapping old-session Object delivery. This is an optional publisher capability; downstream deduplication and ideal seamlessness are relay expectations, not guaranteed by this MAY.

requirements.summary: Include all Track Properties in PUBLISH unless a property's specification permits omission.
requirements.rationale: Section 9.6 assigns preservation of received Track metadata to relays sending PUBLISH; it does not make this occurrence a new original-publisher obligation.

requirements.summary: Include all Track Properties in SUBSCRIBE_OK unless a property's specification permits omission.
requirements.rationale: Preserving Track metadata in a relay's subscription response is independent of its PUBLISH path; the stated actor remains the relay.

requirements.summary: Include all Track Properties in TRACK_STATUS_OK unless a property's specification permits omission.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines TRACK_STATUS_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7, in response to TRACK_STATUS, and explicitly permits Track Properties in that response.
