Preserving all Track Properties remains this relay's duty, subject to each property's omission rules; the defined encoding does not make a relay-only obligation applicable to the original publisher.

requirements.summary: Include all Track Properties in FETCH_OK unless a property's specification permits omission.
requirements.rationale: This is the relay FETCH response metadata-preservation branch, subject to the property-specific rules of Section 2.5.

requirements.summary: Do not modify Object fields when forwarding except Object Properties as allowed by Section 2.5.
requirements.rationale: This constrains the relay forwarding a received canonical Object. It preserves the explicit property exception and does not prohibit an original publisher from initially choosing Object metadata.

requirements.summary: Treat Object payloads as opaque.
requirements.rationale: Payload opacity is a relay handling rule. Section 2.1 explicitly makes the original publisher responsible for encoding and payload contents, so this duty does not forbid publisher payload processing.

requirements.summary: Do not combine Object payloads while relaying.
requirements.rationale: Combining payloads is a specifically prohibited transformation by the relay; this is not the original publisher's content-generation role.

requirements.summary: Do not split Object payloads while relaying.
requirements.rationale: Splitting one incoming payload into multiple Objects is separately forbidden for the relay; the original publisher still chooses initial Object boundaries.

requirements.summary: Do not otherwise modify Object payloads while relaying.
requirements.rationale: This residual prohibition covers relay payload transformations beyond combining and splitting. Publisher Object immutability is a separate rule in Section 2.1.

requirements.summary: Prioritize forwarding Objects according to Section 7.
requirements.rationale: This cross-reference explicitly addresses relay scheduling. Section 7 independently applies publisher scheduling advice, including transport-dependent scheduling semantics; this occurrence remains relay-only.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBE as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: Table 5 marks SUBSCRIBE as Request, First. This sending duty belongs to the subscriber; receiving-side rejection of invalid stream starters is separately specified in Section 3.3.

requirements.summary: Send PUBLISH as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: Table 5 puts PUBLISH on Request, First, not the unidirectional control stream used for SETUP. A peer can inspect the publisher's new stream and first message type.

requirements.summary: Send FETCH as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: Table 5's FETCH sending rule applies to the Object-retrieving subscriber role. A contribution publisher is the FETCH responder in scope here.

requirements.summary: Send TRACK_STATUS as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: Section 2.4.3 expressly identifies TRACK_STATUS as a publisher state-recovery option. If used, Table 5 requires its request to start a new bidirectional stream; the capability itself is not mandatory.

requirements.summary: Send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: The namespace publication request is Request, First in Table 5. Its stream placement is observable independently of whether the relay authorizes the namespace.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: The namespace-discovery requester sends this First message; a contribution publisher can respond to discovery without assuming the subscriber's sending duty.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS as the first message on a new bidirectional request stream.
requirements.rationale: The Track-discovery subscriber initiates this request. Publisher PUBLISH responses use their own new bidirectional streams and are covered by the PUBLISH clause.

requirements.summary: Close the Session after receiving an unknown message type.
requirements.rationale: A publishing endpoint receives protocol messages on control and request streams. An unknown type is fatal even when its length is parseable; this sentence specifies no particular session error code.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when Message Length differs from the Message Payload length.
requirements.rationale: Send a fully delimited known message whose parsed payload does not match its 16-bit length. The publishing receiver's session error is observable; this avoids confusing truncated transport delivery with a completed malformed message.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with INVALID_REQUEST_ID for a Request ID with incorrect sender parity.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.1 assigns even IDs to clients and odd IDs to servers independently of publishing role. A peer request with the wrong low bit exercises a publisher's receive validation.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with INVALID_REQUEST_ID after receiving a duplicate Request ID.
requirements.rationale: Request IDs are allocated per endpoint across requests, including REQUEST_UPDATE, rather than per stream. Reusing an already received ID on another request stream must fail even when each stream's first message and Track are otherwise valid.

requirements.summary: Serialize Message Parameters in ascending Parameter Type order using Type Delta encoding.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH and publisher responses carry Message Parameters. The peer can decode the first absolute type and subsequent deltas; explicitly repeatable types remain allowed under the separate duplicate rule.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when accumulating a Message Parameter Type Delta would exceed 2^64-1.
requirements.rationale: This is receive-side integer-bound validation for publishing endpoints. A valid FORWARD parameter of Type 0x10 followed by a Type Delta of 2^64-1 overflows accumulation without first encountering an unknown parameter type.

requirements.summary: Use only Message Parameters defined by the negotiated MOQT version or negotiated through Setup Options.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's outgoing parameters can be checked against the selected draft and exchanged Setup Options. Merely knowing a private parameter locally does not establish peer negotiation.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after receiving an unknown Message Parameter.
requirements.rationale: Parameters use a count and have no unknown-value skip mechanism. This differs from Setup Options, which have a separate namespace and are ignored when unknown under Section 10.3; the fatal rule must not be applied to unknown Setup Options.

requirements.summary: Do not repeat a Parameter Type in one message unless its definition explicitly permits multiple instances.
requirements.rationale: Outgoing PUBLISH, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE and publisher responses are inspectable. AUTHORIZATION TOKEN is an explicit repeatability exception only when resolved Token Type and Value pairs are unique.

requirements.summary: Check received messages for unexpected duplicate Message Parameters.
requirements.rationale: Performing the check is internal receiver processing. The independently observable recommendation to close the Session after finding a duplicate is recorded in clause 2.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when unexpected duplicate Message Parameters are found.
requirements.rationale: A SUBSCRIBE with two FORWARD parameters supplies a forbidden duplicate to a publisher. Session closure is a SHOULD outcome and does not turn into MUST merely because sender duplication is prohibited.

requirements.summary: Do not alter Object payloads in response to Message Parameters in SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK or FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The named messages are subscriber inputs, but the prohibited action is the publisher changing payload content. Compare the same scoped Track, Group and Object across parameter variants; delivery choices may change while its bytes remain identical under Section 2.4.3.

requirements.summary: Close the connection with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a Message Parameter appears in a message type outside its defined scope.
requirements.rationale: For example, GROUP_ORDER is not allowed in REQUEST_UPDATE. The draft literally says connection here rather than session; a native-QUIC scenario can observe that outcome without inferring teardown of unrelated WebTransport sessions. Setup Options occupy a separate namespace.

requirements.summary: Include AUTHORIZATION TOKEN in PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE, REQUEST_UPDATE, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, TRACK_STATUS or FETCH.
requirements.rationale: This permission includes publisher-originated PUBLISH, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE and updates, as well as subscriber requests. Their wire tokens are observable; it does not permit tokens in arbitrary response messages or prescribe an authorization policy.

requirements.summary: Retire the registered Alias and associated Token Value when processing DELETE.
requirements.rationale: A publisher receiving authorized requests also receives token-cache operations. After successful deletion, a subsequent USE_ALIAS must not resolve the retired mapping; this checks retirement without inspecting cache storage.

requirements.summary: Associate a REGISTER Alias with its Token Value until the Session ends or the alias is deleted.
requirements.rationale: Configure a known token type and authorization policy, register within the advertised cache limit, then authorize a later request through USE_ALIAS. Persistence is observable through request results rather than direct memory inspection. Section 10.3.1.4 defines a SETUP overflow exception.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after receiving DELETE in a SETUP authorization token.
requirements.rationale: This remains applicable to a publisher acting as transport server, and Section 10.3.1.4 imports the Token structure into SETUP. The approved harness is listener-only and the publisher connects as transport client, so the harness cannot exercise a publisher server receiving DELETE in client SETUP. The server-only duty is not broadened to a client receiving server SETUP.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after receiving USE_ALIAS in a SETUP authorization token.
requirements.rationale: The USE_ALIAS prohibition applies independently to a publisher acting as transport server. The approved harness is listener-only and the publisher connects as transport client, so it cannot deliver client SETUP to a publisher server to exercise this duty. Applicability is retained without inventing a client-side rule or an unsupported harness scenario.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with KEY_VALUE_FORMATTING_ERROR when the Token structure cannot be decoded.
requirements.rationale: Inject a valid outer message and parameter length enclosing an incomplete Token structure. This publisher receive error is distinct from an invalid but structurally well-formed token and avoids masking by outer message-length validation.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with DUPLICATE_AUTH_TOKEN_ALIAS when the peer registers an already registered Alias.
requirements.rationale: Register twice in one sender's alias space without deletion, within cache limits. Client and server have independent alias spaces, so an alias used only by the opposite endpoint is not this error.

requirements.summary: Reject a message referencing an unregistered Alias with UNKNOWN_AUTH_TOKEN_ALIAS.
requirements.rationale: A publisher handling token-bearing requests can observe either unknown reference. The draft requires rejection of the message, not termination of the Session as for duplicate registration.

requirements.summary: Reject a structurally well-formed but otherwise invalid AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameter with MALFORMED_AUTH_TOKEN.
requirements.rationale: Use an agreed token type with an invalid value while keeping the outer Token encoding valid. The request-level MALFORMED_AUTH_TOKEN result is distinct from KEY_VALUE_FORMATTING_ERROR and from a valid token lacking authorization.

requirements.summary: Register an AUTHORIZATION TOKEN Alias whenever REGISTER processing does not cause a Session error, even if the request fails for another reason.
requirements.rationale: Send REGISTER within the advertised cache limit on an unauthorized or otherwise rejected request, then USE_ALIAS after its response. The publishing receiver must resolve that alias rather than returning UNKNOWN_AUTH_TOKEN_ALIAS. SETUP overflow has the specific exception in Section 10.3.1.4.

requirements.summary: Store an error code instead of token data only when every future use of the registered alias will produce that error.
requirements.rationale: This optional receiver cache representation is private; the same wire errors result from storing the token or the permanent error. The token's original value length still counts toward cache size, and a token that might become valid must not be treated as permanently invalid.

requirements.summary: Retain a registered Alias after detecting token expiration until the sender deletes it.
requirements.rationale: With a controllable token lifetime, a later USE_ALIAS must produce EXPIRED_AUTH_TOKEN instead of forgetting the alias. Expiration leaves its accounted cache size unchanged; the publisher's stored bytes need not be inspected.

requirements.summary: Discard other no-longer-needed token state after expiration while retaining the Alias and unchanged cache accounting.
requirements.rationale: The optional memory reclamation cannot be distinguished externally from retaining the same state. Wire-visible expiration and Alias lifetime are specified separately and do not prove which data was discarded.

requirements.summary: Register tokens only when intending to reuse them during the Session.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher sends authorization tokens, but its intent to reuse one is internal. Failure to observe later reuse cannot distinguish a violated recommendation from a planned operation that never became necessary.

requirements.summary: Retire registered tokens once their utility has passed.
requirements.rationale: DELETE is observable, but the draft gives no external signal or deadline defining when a publisher's token has no future utility. Wire silence alone cannot establish violation of this application-dependent recommendation.

requirements.summary: Terminate the Session with AUTH_TOKEN_CACHE_OVERFLOW when a token registration would exceed the advertised cache limit.
requirements.rationale: For a token-bearing request, exceed the publishing receiver's limit using 16 bytes plus Token Value length per active entry; zero is the default limit. Section 10.3.1.4 explicitly exempts overflow in SETUP and instead treats that REGISTER as USE_VALUE, so this evaluator excludes SETUP.

requirements.summary: Repeat AUTHORIZATION TOKEN in one message only when each resolved Token Type and Token Value pair is unique.
requirements.rationale: An outgoing publisher request can contain multiple tokens, including alias references. The peer can resolve its registered aliases and check uniqueness; this permission does not require publishers to send multiple tokens.

requirements.summary: Do not send USE_ALIAS on a different control stream from its REGISTER until receiving the REGISTER message's response.
requirements.rationale: This sender rule applies to publisher token use, but the draft says control streams while Section 3.3 gives each sender one control stream and Table 5 places token-bearing requests on request streams. The record preserves the wording; a precise cross-stream wire oracle requires clarification rather than silently substituting request streams.

requirements.summary: Send USE_ALIAS on the same control stream as REGISTER without waiting for a response.
requirements.rationale: The optional publisher sender optimization mentions control streams, whereas Table 5 places the relevant requests and updates on bidirectional request streams. The draft does not resolve that terminology mismatch, so this record does not invent a control-stream permission for request messages.

requirements.summary: Do not send DELETE for an Alias while any USE_ALIAS message for it still awaits a response.
requirements.rationale: After acknowledged registration, hold a publisher USE_ALIAS request response and request retirement. The peer can compare DELETE ordering with outstanding responses; unlike the preceding clauses, this prohibition does not depend on the ambiguous control-stream term.

requirements.summary: Send SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT in PUBLISH_OK, SUBSCRIBE or REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: Section 8 distinguishes subscriber timeout Message Parameters from publisher timeout Track Properties. This MAY permits the subscriber's input; publisher enforcement of effective timeouts is cataloged from Section 8.

requirements.summary: Do not forward SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT upstream when intending to serve multiple subscriptions to the same Track.
requirements.rationale: The relay should keep a subscriber-specific timeout from limiting a shared upstream subscription. The original publisher cannot determine or enforce its peer's aggregation policy.

requirements.summary: Send OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT in PUBLISH_OK, SUBSCRIBE or REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: The parameter is the subscriber's timeout contribution, whereas the publisher supplies a Track Property under Section 8. Receiving and applying the effective timeout does not make the subscriber's MAY a publisher sending duty.

requirements.summary: Do not forward OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT upstream when intending to serve multiple subscriptions to the same Track.
requirements.rationale: This is relay aggregation advice intended to prevent one downstream subscriber's object timeout from affecting others; it does not constrain the original publisher's timeout advertisement.

requirements.summary: Include FILL_TIMEOUT in FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The fetching subscriber optionally supplies the budget for relay upstream retrieval. This is not a parameter the contribution publisher is permitted to place in its FETCH response.

requirements.summary: Limit total waiting for unavailable Objects across upstream FETCHes to FILL_TIMEOUT before reporting remaining unavailable Objects as Unknown gaps.
requirements.rationale: The budget spans all upstream FETCHes generated by the downstream request, not a fresh budget for each. This forwarding relay behavior does not apply to a publisher serving its own Objects.

requirements.summary: Do not wait for upstream delivery when FILL_TIMEOUT is 0.
requirements.rationale: Zero selects only immediately available relay content. The explicit actor is a relay with upstream sources, not an original publisher.

requirements.summary: Report unavailable Objects as Unknown gaps when FILL_TIMEOUT is 0.
requirements.rationale: The relay's missing-content representation is an independent outcome from not waiting; unavailable cached content is not asserted to be permanently nonexistent.

requirements.summary: Use a shorter FILL_TIMEOUT than requested without informing the subscriber when unwilling to wait as long.
requirements.rationale: This is a relay resource-policy permission; no notification or minimum wait is imposed on a contribution publisher by this occurrence.

requirements.summary: Include RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT in SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber requests how long a relay should await an absent publisher. The publisher's eventual appearance does not transfer the subscriber's parameter-sending permission to it.

requirements.summary: Hold a subscription awaiting a publisher for up to RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT when the parameter is present.
requirements.rationale: Rendezvous state is owned by the relay; it withholds SUBSCRIBE_OK until a publisher appears. This does not require a publisher application to buffer requests for other absent publishers.

requirements.summary: Respond with REQUEST_ERROR and TIMEOUT when rendezvous expires without a publisher becoming available.
requirements.rationale: The relay sends this downstream failure after its publisher-wait budget expires; it is not the original publisher's response to a received request.

requirements.summary: Use a shorter rendezvous timeout than the subscriber requested.
requirements.rationale: The relay may limit waiting to protect its resources. The example maximum duration does not establish a fixed timeout for original publishers.

requirements.summary: Immediately return REQUEST_ERROR with DOES_NOT_EXIST when no publisher is available and RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT is 0, including its absent-parameter default.
requirements.rationale: This immediate failure is specifically the relay's zero-wait path. It differs from TIMEOUT after a positive wait and does not classify an original publisher as a relay.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY in SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, a subscription or FETCH REQUEST_UPDATE, or PUBLISH_OK.
requirements.rationale: This permission belongs to the requesting subscriber expressing relative priority. The publisher's default of 128 and Section 7 scheduling semantics describe how it consumes the value, not a publisher permission to send this parameter in responses.

requirements.summary: Send GROUP_ORDER in SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK or FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses this parameter in requests or its PUBLISH response. A publisher communicates its default preference through Track information; its invalid-value receive duty is separately applicable below.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when GROUP_ORDER is neither Ascending (1) nor Descending (2).
requirements.rationale: A publisher receives GROUP_ORDER in SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK and FETCH. Testing both zero and an upper out-of-range value checks the uint8 enumeration without confusing absence, which has separate defaults, with value zero.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIPTION_FILTER in SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK or a subscription REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber sets its desired delivery range. Publisher enforcement and update handling are separate requirements; this sender permission also does not imply omission clears an existing filter on REQUEST_UPDATE.

requirements.summary: Include advisory EXPIRES in SUBSCRIBE_OK.
requirements.rationale: This is an optional publisher response parameter with an observable varint value. Because expiry is advisory, the evaluator does not require termination at the exact advertised instant.

requirements.summary: Include advisory EXPIRES in PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: The original publisher can advertise its intended termination interval when initiating publication. The wire parameter is testable, but the draft permits earlier or later termination.

requirements.summary: Include advisory EXPIRES in PUBLISH_OK.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_OK is sent by the subscriber accepting a publication. The contribution publisher receives this advisory, but this MAY grants the peer's sending permission.

requirements.summary: Include advisory EXPIRES in REQUEST_UPDATE_OK, the REQUEST_OK response to REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as shorthand for a REQUEST_OK response with type 0x7. When the publisher supports expiry renewal and is configured to grant it with an advisory, send an authorized REQUEST_UPDATE on the established subscription stream and inspect its REQUEST_OK for the EXPIRES varint parameter. This optional-capability scenario does not require every publisher to support renewal or terminate at the advertised instant.

requirements.summary: Include available updated AUTHORIZATION_TOKENs in REQUEST_UPDATE when attempting to extend a subscription after receiving EXPIRES.
requirements.rationale: A publisher can receive EXPIRES in PUBLISH_OK and, as the PUBLISH initiator, send REQUEST_UPDATE under Section 10.9. Provide updated credentials and request extension, then inspect that outgoing request. Section 10.5 defines PUBLISH_OK and REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7, identified by their corresponding requests; neither response name has an undefined encoding.

requirements.summary: Introduce jitter when sending EXPIRES to prevent synchronized endpoint updates.
requirements.rationale: The sender-side permission explicitly names relays; it is distinct from the next clause's permission for receiving applications.

requirements.summary: Introduce jitter when acting on received EXPIRES to avoid synchronized updates.
requirements.rationale: A publishing application can receive EXPIRES in PUBLISH_OK. Its jitter choice has no specified distribution or bound, and observed scheduling variation cannot prove intentional jitter rather than transport or application delay.

requirements.summary: Carry LARGEST_OBJECT in SUBSCRIBE_OK.
requirements.rationale: The parameter is permitted in this publisher response and becomes mandatory once Objects have been published. Its Location can be compared with controlled published Objects; absence means no Objects have been published or received.

requirements.summary: Carry LARGEST_OBJECT in PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: The initiating publisher can describe an already active Track's largest Location. This permission is constrained by the following mandatory-presence rule and does not allow an arbitrary Location for an empty Track.

requirements.summary: Carry LARGEST_OBJECT in REQUEST_UPDATE_OK, the REQUEST_OK response to REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7, answering REQUEST_UPDATE. For a publisher supporting and accepting subscription updates, publish Objects to a controlled largest Location, pause new publication, send the update on that subscription stream, and compare LARGEST_OBJECT in its REQUEST_OK with the published Location. The MAY grants parameter carriage, not mandatory feature support; the following MUST separately requires presence after publication.

requirements.summary: Carry LARGEST_OBJECT in TRACK_STATUS_OK, the REQUEST_OK response to TRACK_STATUS.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines TRACK_STATUS_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7, answering TRACK_STATUS. With a publisher supporting and accepting Track status queries, publish Objects to a controlled largest Location, pause new publication, send TRACK_STATUS on a new request stream, and compare the response's LARGEST_OBJECT with that Location. This MAY does not require feature support; successful responses after publication also fall under the separate mandatory-presence clause.

requirements.summary: Include LARGEST_OBJECT in SUBSCRIBE_OK if Objects have been published on the Track.
requirements.rationale: Use actual Object publication rather than queued application data as the precondition and inspect the SUBSCRIBE_OK response for LARGEST_OBJECT. SUBSCRIBE_OK has its own message type; Section 10.5 defines the other listed names REQUEST_UPDATE_OK and TRACK_STATUS_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7. All of these response forms have defined encodings.

requirements.summary: Include LARGEST_OBJECT in PUBLISH if Objects have been published on the Track.
requirements.rationale: Advertise a Track with known published Objects on another subscription and inspect PUBLISH. This mandatory presence is independently testable from SUBSCRIBE_OK; queued but unpublished Objects do not establish the stated precondition.

requirements.summary: Include LARGEST_OBJECT in REQUEST_UPDATE_OK if Objects have been published on the Track.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as shorthand for the REQUEST_OK response, type 0x7, to REQUEST_UPDATE. After observing actual Object publication on an established subscription, send a valid update that the publisher accepts and require LARGEST_OBJECT in the resulting REQUEST_OK on that stream. The obligation is conditional on published Objects and this successful response; it does not require accepting every update.

requirements.summary: Include LARGEST_OBJECT in TRACK_STATUS_OK if Objects have been published on the Track.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines TRACK_STATUS_OK as shorthand for the REQUEST_OK response, type 0x7, to TRACK_STATUS. After observing actual Object publication, query that Track on a new request stream and require LARGEST_OBJECT in an accepted query's REQUEST_OK. This checks mandatory parameter presence in the successful response without requiring acceptance of every Track status query.

requirements.summary: Set LARGEST_OBJECT to the maximum upstream-advertised LARGEST_OBJECT or Object Location received on an upstream subscription.
requirements.rationale: The relay aggregates upstream-advertised Locations and received Object Locations. Section 10.5 defines the listed REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK, type 0x7, responding to REQUEST_UPDATE, so its LARGEST_OBJECT is a defined input to that aggregation. Computing the maximum across upstream inputs remains a relay duty, not an original-publisher duty.

requirements.summary: Include FORWARD in PUBLISH to select initial Forward State; the parameter is also permitted in SUBSCRIBE, subscription REQUEST_UPDATE, PUBLISH_OK and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH is a publisher-originated use of this permission. Sections 5.1 and 10.10 make Forward=0 suppress Objects until the subscriber changes it to 1; omission defaults to 1 except REQUEST_UPDATE omission preserves existing state. Subscriber-originated uses remain valid stimuli, not publisher sending duties.

requirements.summary: Close the Session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after receiving FORWARD outside 0 or 1.
requirements.rationale: A peer can send a well-formed SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK or subscription REQUEST_UPDATE with an invalid uint8 value. The publishing endpoint's session close and error code distinguish rejection from silently treating every nonzero value as 1.

requirements.summary: Send NEW_GROUP_REQUEST in PUBLISH_OK, SUBSCRIBE or a subscription REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: This permission is the subscriber's request for a new Group, subject to the following DYNAMIC_GROUPS restrictions. The original publisher's resulting group-creation recommendation is separately applicable.

requirements.summary: Do not send NEW_GROUP_REQUEST in PUBLISH_OK unless the Track included DYNAMIC_GROUPS with value 1.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber accepting PUBLISH must have observed dynamic-group support before requesting a new Group in that response; this occurrence mandates no publisher rejection code for a violation.

requirements.summary: Do not send NEW_GROUP_REQUEST in REQUEST_UPDATE unless the Track included DYNAMIC_GROUPS with value 1.
requirements.rationale: The update path is a separate subscriber sending restriction. Original publishers indicate support using the Track Property; they are not the senders constrained here.

requirements.summary: Include NEW_GROUP_REQUEST in SUBSCRIBE without prior knowledge of dynamic-group support.
requirements.rationale: The explicit exception belongs to a subscriber initiating subscription. The following non-keyword sentence says an unsupported original publisher ignores it; this MAY is not a new publisher sending permission.

requirements.summary: End the current Group as soon as practical after receiving NEW_GROUP_REQUEST=0 or a value above the current Group when dynamic Groups are supported.
requirements.rationale: Group termination can be observed in Object status or the stream's End-of-Group signaling. The draft allows implementation-specific delay, so the evaluator identifies the transition without inventing a fixed response deadline or requiring a particular next Group ID.

requirements.summary: Begin a new Group as soon as practical after receiving NEW_GROUP_REQUEST=0 or a value above the current Group when dynamic Groups are supported.
requirements.rationale: A controlled dynamic Track with continued media can expose Objects in the next Group independently of ending the old Group. There is no requirement to equal the requested Group ID and no protocol-defined maximum delay; those are not asserted.

requirements.summary: Delay acting on NEW_GROUP_REQUEST for implementation-specific concerns such as a minimum Group duration.
requirements.rationale: The optional delay is justified by private implementation concerns without a required duration or response signal. Observed latency alone cannot identify that policy or distinguish it from scheduling delay, so this permission has no independent external oracle.

requirements.summary: Include a received NEW_GROUP_REQUEST when subscribing upstream for a Track without an Established subscription.
requirements.rationale: This relay propagation rule makes the request visible to an original publisher, but the upstream request construction belongs to the relay. It is the new-subscription path, distinct from REQUEST_UPDATE below.

requirements.summary: For an Established subscription, send REQUEST_UPDATE with NEW_GROUP_REQUEST=0 or above the Largest Group unless dynamic Groups are unsupported or an equal-or-larger request is already outstanding.
requirements.rationale: Only the relay maintains this outstanding upstream request state and aggregates subscriber demand. Both enumerated exceptions remain part of the trigger; the original publisher's response recommendation is a different occurrence.

requirements.summary: Include TRACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX in REQUEST_UPDATE for SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS to change the subscribed prefix.
requirements.rationale: The namespace or Track-discovery subscriber chooses this updated prefix. Publisher receive-side overlap validation is separately applicable in the next occurrence.

requirements.summary: Respond REQUEST_ERROR with PREFIX_OVERLAP if a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE prefix update overlaps another active SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE in the same Session.
requirements.rationale: Sections 10.18 and 10.9.2 identify the publisher as responder to namespace discovery and updates. Two active subscriptions of the same type establish the conflict; a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS subscription alone is outside this overlap space.

requirements.summary: Respond REQUEST_ERROR with PREFIX_OVERLAP if a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS prefix update overlaps another active SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS in the same Session.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.19 permits an original publisher to serve Track discovery. Its active SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS prefixes form an independent overlap space from SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, so the second validation path needs its own stimulus.

requirements.summary: Pipeline other control messages after SETUP without waiting for peer SETUP when not offering extensions that modify control-message semantics.
requirements.rationale: The permission concerns the endpoint sending SETUP; observe its control stream while the listener delays its own SETUP. Optional pipelining is not mandatory support.

requirements.summary: Ignore unknown Setup Options.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher receives peer SETUP; use otherwise valid options and continue a valid request to establish that the unknown option did not alter semantics.

requirements.summary: Ignore unrecognized Setup Options in their version-independent namespace.
requirements.rationale: This repeats the extensibility requirement at line 3521 and remains a separate lexical anchor; Message Parameter unknown-value rules do not apply.

requirements.summary: Do not repeat a Setup Option Type unless its definition explicitly permits multiple instances.
requirements.rationale: Inspect the publisher SETUP. Section 10.3.1.4 permits multiple authorization tokens; this sender constraint does not prescribe a receiver error for duplicate known options.

requirements.summary: Allow duplicate instances of unknown Setup Options.
requirements.rationale: Exercise duplicate unknown Option Types, independently of known-option repetition and Message Parameter validation.

requirements.summary: Do not send AUTHORITY as a transport server.
requirements.rationale: Publisher and server are independent roles, so this is conditionally applicable. The listener-only runner accepts a publishing transport client and cannot observe a publisher acting as server.

requirements.summary: Do not send AUTHORITY over WebTransport.
requirements.rationale: The publisher is the WebTransport client; AUTHORITY is supplied by the transport and cannot be repeated as a Setup Option.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_AUTHORITY on receiving AUTHORITY from a server.
requirements.rationale: Send a syntactically valid AUTHORITY from the listener to isolate the prohibited sender role.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_AUTHORITY on receiving AUTHORITY over WebTransport.
requirements.rationale: The publisher as WebTransport client can receive this invalid option from the runner; use a syntactically valid value.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_AUTHORITY when the client's specified authority is unsupported.
requirements.rationale: The supported-authority check is a transport-server duty. A publishing server is conditionally covered, but the listener-only runner cannot connect as its client.

requirements.summary: Set AUTHORITY to the authority component of the moqt connection URI.
requirements.rationale: Configure a native QUIC publisher URI and compare the emitted AUTHORITY with that URI component, using the Section 3.1.4 mapping.

requirements.summary: Close the session with MALFORMED_AUTHORITY when AUTHORITY violates its URI formatting rules.
requirements.rationale: A role-valid AUTHORITY travels from native QUIC client to server. This runner only receives publisher connections; sending malformed AUTHORITY to its client also violates the sender-role rule requiring INVALID_AUTHORITY, and the draft defines no error precedence.

requirements.summary: Do not send PATH as a transport server.
requirements.rationale: The transport-server role is conditionally applicable to a publisher, but cannot be exercised by the listener-only runner.

requirements.summary: Do not send PATH over WebTransport.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publisher's WebTransport SETUP can be inspected directly for the prohibited option.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_PATH on receiving PATH from a server.
requirements.rationale: Use a well-formed PATH sent by the listener to isolate the prohibited server role.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_PATH on receiving PATH over WebTransport.
requirements.rationale: A well-formed PATH over WebTransport is invalid independently of its contents.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_PATH when the client's specified path is unsupported.
requirements.rationale: This is a server validation duty, conditionally applicable to a publishing server. The approved runner listens for client publishers and cannot exercise that role.

requirements.summary: Set PATH to the path-abempty component when connecting to a moqt URI.
requirements.rationale: Configure a native QUIC URI with a known path; compare the publisher SETUP PATH against that component, including an empty path case.

requirements.summary: Append a question mark followed by the query component to PATH when the moqt URI has a query.
requirements.rationale: The query delimiter and query bytes are observable in the client publisher's SETUP, including a present but empty query.

requirements.summary: Close the session with MALFORMED_PATH when PATH violates its URI formatting rules.
requirements.rationale: A role-valid PATH is received by a native QUIC server. The listener-only runner cannot exercise a publishing server; sending malformed PATH to the publisher client also triggers INVALID_PATH, with no specified precedence.

requirements.summary: Do not fail SETUP with AUTH_TOKEN_CACHE_OVERFLOW when a REGISTER token exceeds MAX_AUTH_TOKEN_CACHE_SIZE.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.3.1.4 explicitly overrides the general registration overflow rule in Section 10.2.2. Send a valid token exceeding the advertised or default zero limit.

requirements.summary: Treat a SETUP REGISTER token exceeding the cache limit as USE_VALUE.
requirements.rationale: Use known authorization policy and token bytes, then reference the would-be alias on a request. USE_VALUE authenticates using the value without registering that alias; Section 10.2.2 defines the subsequent unknown-alias outcome.

requirements.summary: Purge locally remembered Token Aliases whose SETUP registration failed under the peer's advertised or default zero cache limit.
requirements.rationale: Purging sender memory is internal. A later value-based token use does not prove deletion, and the runner cannot require the application to reuse every failed alias.

requirements.summary: Encode MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION as a UTF-8 string.
requirements.rationale: When the optional identification value is sent, its byte encoding is directly observable; no language-tag or display-comprehension requirement is added.

requirements.summary: Send MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION unless specifically configured not to do so.
requirements.rationale: The driven scenario establishes that identification has not been disabled. Absence under unknown configuration is not a conformance failure.

requirements.summary: Limit MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION to the implementation name and version, avoiding nonessential information.
requirements.rationale: The draft provides no grammar or objective boundary for names, versions, advertising and essential information; a wire evaluator must not invent one.

requirements.summary: Do not use another implementation's identifier to declare compatibility.
requirements.rationale: The wire string alone does not establish ownership of an identifier or intent to claim compatibility. The draft supplies no authoritative identity registry.

requirements.summary: Send a zero-length New Session URI in every client GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: Applies to both control and request stream GOAWAY sent by the publishing transport client.

requirements.summary: Send GOAWAY on a request stream to initiate migration of that request.
requirements.rationale: The permission is observable when supported by the publisher; it does not require optional request migration support.

requirements.summary: On request-stream GOAWAY, reissue that specific request at the specified URI or on the current session if no URI is supplied.
requirements.rationale: Use PUBLISH or PUBLISH_NAMESPACE initiated by the contribution publisher, so it owns the request. This sentence explicitly says current session for an empty request URI; do not replace it with the control-stream migration rule.

requirements.summary: On request-stream GOAWAY, close the old request stream using its appropriate completion or cancellation mechanism.
requirements.rationale: Observe FIN/reset for a namespace request or PUBLISH_DONE and closure for a publication. These are examples of suitable mechanisms, not a mandate to use every mechanism.

requirements.summary: Individually unsubscribe existing subscriptions after GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: The actor is the subscriber relinquishing subscriptions, not the contribution publisher. The draft's uppercase UNSUBSCRIBE is descriptive here; its cancellation mechanism is specified in Section 3.3.2.

requirements.summary: Reject new requests after sending GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: This general permission must be read with the mandatory GOING_AWAY rejections for a control-stream GOAWAY cutoff later in this section.

requirements.summary: Do not initiate new requests to the peer after receiving control-stream GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: Observe publisher-originated PUBLISH and PUBLISH_NAMESPACE on the draining session; migrating requests to a replacement session remains permitted.

requirements.summary: Avoid initiating new requests after sending GOAWAY unless required for migration.
requirements.rationale: A driven scenario distinguishes a newly requested publication from requests required by migration. Sending GOAWAY does not absolutely prohibit new requests.

requirements.summary: Reject new requests with an appropriate error after receiving GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: GOING_AWAY is given as an example, not an exclusive mandatory code for this permission. Observe a valid request rejection.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a second GOAWAY on the control stream.
requirements.rationale: Duplicate counting is per control stream; the publisher receives two GOAWAY messages on the same peer stream.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a second GOAWAY on one request stream.
requirements.rationale: Separate request streams may each carry one GOAWAY. The duplicate stimulus deliberately uses the same active request stream.

requirements.summary: Use a provided GOAWAY New Session URI for the replacement session.
requirements.rationale: Provide a reachable listener URI and observe the client publisher's replacement connection. This does not require migration to an unspecified destination.

requirements.summary: Use the current URI scheme in the GOAWAY New Session URI.
requirements.rationale: Only a server can send a nonempty GOAWAY URI; clients must send an empty one. Publishing-server behavior is outside this listener-only harness.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if GOAWAY New Session URI exceeds 8192 bytes.
requirements.rationale: Use a well-framed GOAWAY with a declared URI length above the explicit maximum, avoiding an unrelated framing error.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on client GOAWAY with nonempty New Session URI.
requirements.rationale: The publishing endpoint can in principle act as a server, but the runner accepts publishing clients and cannot send this client-only violation to a publisher server.

requirements.summary: Reset a GOAWAY request stream with GOING_AWAY after its nonzero Timeout expires.
requirements.rationale: Use an advertised nonzero timeout and leave the request open. The permission to close earlier in this paragraph means an earlier valid reset is not a timing failure.

requirements.summary: Migrate as quickly as possible when a GOAWAY Timeout is zero.
requirements.rationale: The draft provides no objective deadline for as quickly as possible, and local readiness and application migration costs are not visible at the protocol boundary.

requirements.summary: Close the session before the GOAWAY Timeout elapses.
requirements.rationale: The timeout is a hint, not a minimum guaranteed session lifetime. This optional behavior can be observed on the runner's transport.

requirements.summary: Reset the request stream before its GOAWAY Timeout elapses.
requirements.rationale: This separate optional request-stream outcome does not imply the whole session must close.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_REQUEST_ID if the control GOAWAY cutoff Request ID has the wrong receiver parity.
requirements.rationale: The GOAWAY field identifies the receiver's own requests, unlike ordinary incoming request IDs. For a client publisher its parity must be the client's parity from Section 10.1.

requirements.summary: Reject requests at or above the sent control GOAWAY Request ID cutoff with REQUEST_ERROR GOING_AWAY.
requirements.rationale: This clause governs the endpoint that sent the cutoff, not the endpoint receiving its own request IDs. Establish pending peer requests and inspect the responses.

requirements.summary: Reject requests arriving after sending control GOAWAY with REQUEST_ERROR GOING_AWAY.
requirements.rationale: The post-GOAWAY arrival condition is independent of the numeric cutoff. The earlier general MAY does not remove this explicit control-stream requirement.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if PUBLISH_OK carries Track Properties.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines PUBLISH_OK as REQUEST_OK in reply to PUBLISH. Use that wire message; Track Properties are only populated for TRACK_STATUS_OK in this format.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if REQUEST_UPDATE_OK carries Track Properties.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 explicitly defines REQUEST_UPDATE_OK as REQUEST_OK responding to REQUEST_UPDATE. A publisher can initiate an update to its own PUBLISH or PUBLISH_NAMESPACE request under Section 10.9.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE_OK carries Track Properties.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE_OK as REQUEST_OK replying to namespace discovery; receiving it is the subscriber role. The enumerated sentence does not mention SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS_OK, so no extra prohibition is invented.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_OK carries Track Properties.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_OK as REQUEST_OK in reply to the publisher's namespace announcement. Do not confuse this with TRACK_STATUS_OK, where Track Properties are allowed.

requirements.summary: Use the current session URI when a Redirect has zero-length Connect URI.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is a publisher-initiated request allowed to receive REDIRECT under Section 10.6.2. This URI recommendation does not require a new connection if the current one can be used.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a Redirect with nonempty Connect URI received as server.
requirements.rationale: The server-role restriction is conditionally applicable, but the listener-only harness receives a client publisher. A nonempty Redirect from this server to that client is allowed.

requirements.summary: Leave Redirect Track Name empty when redirecting SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: A publisher may respond to namespace discovery with a Redirect. This is a constraint on the serialized response when that optional redirection is used.

requirements.summary: Leave Redirect Track Name empty when redirecting PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is received by the subscriber or relay; originating its redirect is not a contribution publisher duty.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE Redirect with nonempty Track Name.
requirements.rationale: The receiving requester is the namespace subscriber, not the publisher serving discovery.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Redirect with nonempty Track Name.
requirements.rationale: The runner can return a correctly framed REDIRECT to the publisher's namespace announcement with the forbidden Track Name.

requirements.summary: Wait at least Retry Interval minus one milliseconds before retrying a request when Retry Interval is nonzero.
requirements.rationale: Use a publisher-originated namespace request and a Retry Interval larger than one. The encoded plus-one convention makes value 1 immediately retryable; no retry is mandated.

requirements.summary: Do not retry a request rejected with Retry Interval zero.
requirements.rationale: Drive the same publication intent after a terminal REQUEST_ERROR and observe whether the unchanged request is retried; a materially changed request is not the same retry.

requirements.summary: Select a relevant REQUEST_ERROR code from the defined and registered meanings.
requirements.rationale: This is advice to the application. The generic choice of a relevant code depends on application failure reasons that the wire cannot establish. Explicit error mappings elsewhere remain separately testable.

requirements.summary: Reject new requests after receiving GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: The GOING_AWAY error description repeats the Section 10.4 permission and gets its own lexical record without turning it into a requirement to reject.

requirements.summary: Use Retry Interval to indicate when an EXCESSIVE_LOAD request can be retried.
requirements.rationale: Condition on the publisher rejecting a request with EXCESSIVE_LOAD that is retryable with the same parameters. Lines 3877-3882 require a nonzero Retry Interval for retryable requests; inspect that the response carries a positive value, including 1 for immediate retry. This does not predict actual overload recovery, require recovery by the advertised time, or prescribe a fixed interval.

requirements.summary: On REDIRECT, establish a session at the supplied Connect URI when one is present.
requirements.rationale: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is the listed contribution-publisher request to which REDIRECT can apply. Use a reachable replacement listener; do not extend REDIRECT to PUBLISH, which the list omits.

requirements.summary: Retry the redirected request using the supplied name components when present.
requirements.rationale: For PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, Section 10.6.1 requires empty Track Name and supplies the new namespace. Empty namespace and name retain the original values.

requirements.summary: Forward an upstream REDIRECT to matching downstream requests.
requirements.rationale: This is relay fanout behavior, not an original publisher's handling of its own redirect.

requirements.summary: Cache a Full Track Name REDIRECT for up to Retry Interval milliseconds and answer matching requests from it.
requirements.rationale: This is an optional relay cache operation. Preserve the stated Retry Interval milliseconds cache limit without replacing it with the retry-wait minus-one encoding.

requirements.summary: Reply to a successful SUBSCRIBE with SUBSCRIBE_OK.
requirements.rationale: The reply is on the SUBSCRIBE request stream and is exclusive with REQUEST_ERROR under Section 5.1; Section 10.8 identifies it as the first response.

requirements.summary: Start sending Objects for a successful subscription when its Forward State and filter permit delivery.
requirements.rationale: The conjunction adds an independently observable delivery action. Section 5.1 prohibits data when Forward State is zero; do not turn this sentence into unconditional delivery or delivery of past Objects.

requirements.summary: Respond to an individually processed REQUEST_UPDATE with exactly one REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: A publisher receives subscriber updates to subscriptions and discovery requests. Section 10.9.1 expressly permits one error for a failed coalesced batch, so this single-update scenario does not contradict that exception.

requirements.summary: When a subscription REQUEST_UPDATE fails, also terminate that subscription with PUBLISH_DONE UPDATE_FAILED.
requirements.rationale: Observe the request error and PUBLISH_DONE status on that subscription stream; do not merely accept an error response while the subscription remains live.

requirements.summary: Reset the FETCH data stream when its REQUEST_UPDATE fails.
requirements.rationale: The independent data-stream cleanup is externally visible. The sentence does not prescribe a reset error code, so none is invented.

requirements.summary: Close the bidirectional stream when a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE REQUEST_UPDATE fails.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publisher is the namespace-discovery responder. This clause does not name SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS; its omission is retained rather than filled in.

requirements.summary: Close the bidirectional stream when a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE REQUEST_UPDATE fails.
requirements.rationale: The responder to PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is the namespace receiver, not the publisher originating that request.

requirements.summary: Coalesce REQUEST_UPDATE processing on one stream by applying the cumulative result with later values overriding earlier ones.
requirements.rationale: Whether intermediate states were processed is internal and not proved by the final state. The independent externally visible response requirement is recorded at line 4124; a coalesced failure has one REQUEST_ERROR per lines 4126-4129.

requirements.summary: Send REQUEST_OK for each successful update even when processing a cumulative batch.
requirements.rationale: Section 10.5 defines the REQUEST_UPDATE_OK shorthand as REQUEST_OK. The distinct failure case allows a single REQUEST_ERROR for a failed coalesced batch and is not evaluated as missing per-update successes.

requirements.summary: Do not update a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE prefix to overlap another active SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE in the session.
requirements.rationale: The sentence constrains the namespace subscriber's updated prefix. The publisher's required PREFIX_OVERLAP response is separately stated in Section 10.2.14; the two discovery types have independent overlap spaces.

requirements.summary: Do not update a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS prefix to overlap another active SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS in the session.
requirements.rationale: This parallel sender constraint concerns track-discovery subscribers. Do not prohibit overlap with SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, whose overlap space is independent.

requirements.summary: Respond to an unwanted PUBLISH with REQUEST_ERROR UNINTERESTED.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber rejects a contribution; this is not a duty of the publisher sending PUBLISH.

requirements.summary: Abandon reading streams associated with an unwanted PUBLISH using STOP_SENDING.
requirements.rationale: This independent subscriber cancellation action is split from its request-error response. It is not a publisher obligation.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH_DONE until all data streams that will ever be opened for the subscription have been closed.
requirements.rationale: Section 5.1.1 and the request-stream FIN rule at lines 4236-4237 establish the data-stream scope. Relative arrival order across independent streams cannot establish sender close-before-PUBLISH_DONE ordering; publisher-side transport evidence would be required. The prose at line 4217 inconsistently calls PUBLISH_DONE a control-stream message.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH_DONE while any datagrams remain to be sent for the subscription.
requirements.rationale: Remaining sender datagram work is internal. Late datagram arrival is explicitly allowed by this section and cannot prove a datagram was sent after PUBLISH_DONE; absence cannot prove the queue was empty.

requirements.summary: Do not destroy subscription state before sending PUBLISH_DONE.
requirements.rationale: The allocation lifetime of subscription state is internal. Observed protocol responsiveness is only a proxy and cannot prove the state was retained or destroyed at the required instant.

requirements.summary: Send FIN on the subscription bidirectional stream immediately after PUBLISH_DONE.
requirements.rationale: Same-stream ordering and FIN are observable; immediate means the final response is followed by closure without an invented wall-clock threshold.

requirements.summary: After PUBLISH_DONE, set a timer at least as long as the larger subgroup or object delivery timeout.
requirements.rationale: This is receiver retention for late Objects and does not constrain the publishing contribution endpoint.

requirements.summary: Omit the late-object timer after unsubscribing or losing interest in the track.
requirements.rationale: The permission belongs to the Object receiver's cleanup policy.

requirements.summary: Discard subscription state early at the cost of losing late Objects.
requirements.rationale: The stated tradeoff belongs to the subscriber delivering Objects to its application, not the sender.

requirements.summary: Send STOP_SENDING on all related streams when deleting subscription state.
requirements.rationale: This is subscriber stream cleanup following PUBLISH_DONE.

requirements.summary: Set PUBLISH_DONE Stream Count to zero if no streams were opened for the subscription.
requirements.rationale: Use a driven subscription with Forward State zero and no data streams; inspect the Stream Count in its final PUBLISH_DONE.

requirements.summary: Set PUBLISH_DONE Stream Count to 2^62 - 1 when unable to provide the exact opened-stream count.
requirements.rationale: The inability to compute an exact count is an internal condition the protocol cannot trigger or prove. Observing the sentinel alone does not establish whether it was required.

requirements.summary: Use a timeout or another mechanism to remove state despite an incorrect, unidentifiable-stream, or maximum Stream Count.
requirements.rationale: The second keyword on line 4284 advises the subscriber's cleanup mechanism; it is independent of the publisher sentinel requirement.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if received streams exceed PUBLISH_DONE Stream Count.
requirements.rationale: The Object receiver may police the count; the publisher sending it is not the actor.

requirements.summary: Choose a relevant PUBLISH_DONE status code for ending the subscription.
requirements.rationale: The generic application reason cannot be derived solely from the wire and the draft gives no exhaustive decision algorithm. Specific triggers such as UPDATE_FAILED are evaluated by their own requirements.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on FETCH Type outside 0x1, 0x2 and 0x3.
requirements.rationale: The publisher receives Standalone, Relative Joining or Absolute Joining FETCH. Send an otherwise well-framed request with an unrecognized discriminator.

requirements.summary: Reject a Joining FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_RANGE unless the associated subscription has Forward State 1.
requirements.rationale: Establish a valid subscription with Forward State zero before the fetch. Section 10.12.2 excludes this state even if the referenced subscription and requested Objects otherwise exist.

requirements.summary: Process pending updates to the associated subscription before evaluating its Joining FETCH.
requirements.rationale: Deliver an update that changes Forward State before the joining request, retaining evidence that both complete messages reached the endpoint. Evaluate the updated state and Joining Location from Section 5.1; this does not require a particular inter-stream response arrival order.

requirements.summary: Reject a Joining FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_RANGE if no Objects have been published for the track.
requirements.rationale: Use an existing Forward State one subscription with no published Objects, independently of the separate Forward State zero rejection.

requirements.summary: Reject a Joining FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_JOINING_REQUEST_ID unless its ID refers to a same-session subscription in Established or Pending (subscriber) state.
requirements.rationale: Exercise a non-subscription ID, a different-session ID and a Pending (publisher) subscription. Preserve Pending (subscriber) as allowed: the error-description text at lines 3970-3971 mentions only Established, while this detailed rule and lines 4394-4400 expressly permit Pending.

requirements.summary: Start delivering FETCH Objects immediately from the cached beginning of the range.
requirements.rationale: This permission requires a relay cache and does not define an original publisher's delivery schedule.

requirements.summary: Pause later FETCH delivery at an uncached Object with unknown status until its upstream status is confirmed.
requirements.rationale: The actor resolves cache gaps from an upstream publisher; the contribution publisher is not that relay.

requirements.summary: Specify an End Location no smaller than Start Location for a Standalone FETCH.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber constructs both request fields. This sentence supplies a range validity constraint, not a specified publisher error response. Lines 4389-4390 define the encoded end as last Object plus one, despite this paragraph calling the range inclusive.

requirements.summary: Choose an Absolute Joining FETCH whose derived End Location is no smaller than its Start Location.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses Joining Start; Section 10.12.2.1 computes the corresponding locations from subscription state. The constraint does not prescribe a publisher error for violating it, and no such response is invented. Relative Joining underflow is also not specified here.

requirements.summary: Reject FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_RANGE if no Objects have been published for the track.
requirements.rationale: This general FETCH rule is distinct from the Joining FETCH no-content anchor at line 4441.

requirements.summary: Reject FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_RANGE if Start Location exceeds the Largest Object.
requirements.rationale: Establish a known Largest Object through driven publication and request a lexicographically greater Start Location. Do not conflate this explicit rejection with the underspecified reversed-end case at line 4567.

requirements.summary: Send fetched groups in the requested ascending or descending Group Order.
requirements.rationale: The single FETCH stream preserves observable byte order. Section 10.2.8 defines Group Order; within-group Object ID order is stated in the following sentence and Subgroup ID is not the ordering key.

requirements.summary: Send FETCH Objects before sending FETCH_OK.
requirements.rationale: The optional permission concerns send ordering between the data and request streams. Peer arrival ordering cannot establish which was sent first, so a protocol-only runner must not claim it proves this capability.

requirements.summary: Do not send FETCH_OK until its End Location is known.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's knowledge at the send instant is internal. The reported End Location and delivered range can be validated elsewhere, but a plausible final value does not establish when it became known.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if FETCH_OK End Location is below the corresponding FETCH Start Location.
requirements.rationale: The receiver is the FETCH subscriber. This is not the publisher's response to an invalid incoming FETCH range.

requirements.summary: Without an Established subscription, forward TRACK_STATUS to one or more publishers.
requirements.rationale: This is an upstream relay request permission. The publisher's TRACK_STATUS response behavior at lines 4663-4671 contains no owned normative keyword; Section 10.5 nevertheless defines TRACK_STATUS_OK as REQUEST_OK, so it is not an undefined message.

requirements.summary: Without an Established subscription, initiate an authorized subscription to determine a TRACK_STATUS response.
requirements.rationale: This alternative relay strategy is distinct from forwarding TRACK_STATUS. It does not require the original publisher to create a subscription in response to TRACK_STATUS; lines 4663-4667 say the opposite.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE has more than 32 namespace fields.
requirements.rationale: Send a structurally complete namespace-discovery request with a 33-field prefix; the example namespaces are explanatory and add no naming constraints.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if the first SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE response is neither REQUEST_OK nor REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: This policing action belongs to the subscriber. The publisher's first-response exclusivity is separately normative in Section 6.1 lines 2223-2225, outside this partition.

requirements.summary: Reject a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE prefix overlapping an established SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE in the session with REQUEST_ERROR PREFIX_OVERLAP.
requirements.rationale: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS have independent overlap spaces. Exercise exact, ancestor and descendant prefix overlap within the same request type without treating a cross-type match as this error trigger.

requirements.summary: Ensure the subscriber is authorized for the requested namespace subscription.
requirements.rationale: Use a driven publisher with a known deny policy and credentials to establish the condition. Observe no successful unauthorized namespace subscription; this clause does not specify a unique failure code or mandate a particular authorization backend.

requirements.summary: Do not send NAMESPACE_DONE for a suffix before its corresponding NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: Both messages use the discovery response stream, so their ordering is directly observable. Match suffixes relative to the active prefix, including prefix updates defined in Section 10.9.2.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on NAMESPACE_DONE before the corresponding NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber detects publisher ordering errors; it is not a response the contribution publisher must send.

requirements.summary: Reset the SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE response stream when flow control prevents timely NAMESPACE or NAMESPACE_DONE delivery.
requirements.rationale: The runner can withhold stream credit while driven namespace changes queue output and observe an optional reset. No fixed timeliness threshold, reset code or mandatory reset capability is imposed.

requirements.summary: Treat reset or FIN of a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE response stream as NAMESPACE_DONE for every active namespace.
requirements.rationale: This updates subscriber discovery state. The paragraph explicitly preserves subscriptions established on separate PUBLISH streams.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS has more than 32 namespace fields.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publisher receives track-discovery requests; the limit is independently stated for this request type.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if the first SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS response is neither REQUEST_OK nor REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: The keyword's sentence crosses a page break. The subscriber enforces this rule; publisher response and subsequent PUBLISH behavior are stated here in lowercase prose and in Section 6.1's earlier normative anchor.

requirements.summary: Reject a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS prefix overlapping an established SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS in the session with REQUEST_ERROR PREFIX_OVERLAP.
requirements.rationale: The overlap space is independent of SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE. Apply matching only against established track-discovery subscriptions in this session.

requirements.summary: Ensure the subscriber is authorized for the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS namespace subscription.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's authorization duty applies before accepting track discovery. Use a known deny policy to observe rejection without requiring a particular backend or inventing an error code from this sentence.

requirements.summary: Close the session when receiving an unknown datagram type.
requirements.rationale: Datagram type dispatch applies to every endpoint, including a contribution publisher. Send a type other than the Object Datagram and Padding types; Section 11 does not mandate a specific error code.

requirements.summary: Use both Subgroups and Datagrams for different Objects within one Group.
requirements.rationale: The permission is the Original Publisher's choice under Sections 2.1-2.3. Observe distinct Objects in one Group on a Subgroup stream and in Object Datagrams; optional mixed delivery is not mandatory feature support.

requirements.summary: Use both Subgroups and Datagrams for Objects within one Track.
requirements.rationale: The Track-level permission is independently observable even when individual Groups use a single preference. Correlate received Track Alias with the established Track and preserve each Object's individual preference.

requirements.summary: Do not use the same Track Alias for two different Tracks simultaneously in the same session.
requirements.rationale: Inspect PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE_OK assignments while both subscriptions are Established. The rule is simultaneous and session-scoped, not a ban on reuse after retirement; Section 11.1 notes that old Objects can remain in flight after cancellation.

requirements.summary: Close the session with DUPLICATE_TRACK_ALIAS when PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE_OK reuses an alias of a different Track with an Established subscription.
requirements.rationale: The collision detector is explicitly the subscriber. A contribution publisher assigns its aliases; its sending-side prohibition is the separate anchor at line 4962. Receiving this error is not itself a publisher duty.

requirements.summary: Retain enough cancelled-subscription state to quickly discard late unwanted Objects instead of treating their aliases as unknown.
requirements.rationale: This state-retention recommendation is explicitly for subscribers receiving late Objects. The listener exercises that role; the contribution publisher does not acquire the subscriber obligation.

requirements.summary: Send an Object in a subscription according to that Object's assigned Forwarding Preference.
requirements.rationale: Sections 11.3 and 11.4.2 explicitly establish the preference of an Object observed in an Object Datagram or Subgroup stream. For a publisher supporting repeated delivery, use that first observation as independent evidence when evaluating the same Object on a later subscription. Section 2.4.2 rejects changed preference for the same Object; Section 10.12.3 exempts FETCH transport, so the evaluator never requires a FETCH response to use datagrams.

requirements.summary: Do not process the opaque Object payload intended for an End Subscriber.
requirements.rationale: This is explicitly a relay processing restriction. The Original Publisher is responsible for payload content under Section 2.1 and is not prohibited from processing its own payload.

requirements.summary: Cache Normal, End of Group and End of Track Object status information.
requirements.rationale: The paragraph enumerates statuses learned from subscription Objects; caching these received signals is a subscriber/cache function. It does not require the Original Publisher to cache its own outgoing status signals.

requirements.summary: Treat an Object Status other than Normal 0x0, End of Group 0x3 or End of Track 0x4 as a protocol error.
requirements.rationale: This concerns validation of received subscription Objects, which Section 11.2 says publishers send. The contribution publisher has no receiving subscription in this scope; session closure is separately recommended at line 5056.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for an Object Status outside 0x0, 0x3 and 0x4.
requirements.rationale: The receiver of an Object performs this response. The SHOULD is retained rather than strengthened to MUST; the publisher's outgoing payload restriction at line 5057 is a separate requirement.

requirements.summary: Give every Object whose status is nonzero an empty payload.
requirements.rationale: Inspect publisher-sent status Objects using the Subgroup and Datagram encodings in Sections 11.3.1 and 11.4.2. Nonzero status cannot carry payload; zero-length Normal Objects remain legal.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on receiving Properties on an Object whose status is not Normal.
requirements.rationale: Although phrased as an endpoint rule, its trigger is receiving an Object on a subscription, a subscriber role under Sections 11 and 11.2. Sending malformed Objects to an original contribution publisher with no receiving subscription cannot establish this role-specific trigger.

requirements.summary: Serialize Object metadata never intended for transport or relay access in the Object payload instead of an Object Property.
requirements.rationale: The publisher chooses metadata placement, but whether particular metadata was ever intended for transport or relay access is application intent. This harness treats payloads as opaque and cannot infer that intent from wire bytes.

requirements.summary: Drop a received Object Datagram whose Track Alias is unknown.
requirements.rationale: This is a receiving-subscription behavior. It permits dropping before alias establishment and does not require a contribution publisher to act as an Object consumer.

requirements.summary: Buffer a received Object Datagram with an unknown Track Alias briefly to allow reordering with the establishing control message.
requirements.rationale: This is the alternative subscriber behavior to dropping the unknown-alias datagram. The draft gives no numeric definition of brief; no timeout is invented.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when an Object Datagram has PROPERTIES set but Properties Length is zero.
requirements.rationale: The field validation is performed while receiving Object Datagrams as a subscriber. It is distinct from type dispatch, which every endpoint performs. Section 11.3 permits unknown-alias Objects to be dropped, so such input cannot prove this publisher receiver path.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for an Object Datagram type having both STATUS 0x20 and END_OF_GROUP 0x02 set.
requirements.rationale: The type is invalid before any Track Alias or Object field is parsed, so the endpoint-as-publisher can receive this stimulus without a receiving subscription. The eight expressly listed types exercise the reserved combination.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for an invalid Object Datagram type outside 0x00..0x0F and 0x20..0x2F.
requirements.rationale: The type check is observable before Track Alias processing. The literal outside-range wording overlaps the separately defined Padding Datagram type in Section 11.5.2; preserve that discrepancy and use 0x10, not valid padding, as the unambiguous invalid stimulus. No rejection of the defined padding production is inferred.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for an Object Datagram with STATUS and PROPERTIES set and a non-Normal Object Status.
requirements.rationale: This is subscription Object validation by its receiving endpoint, restating Section 11.2.1.2 for the Datagram form. A contribution publisher's outgoing traffic does not transfer the subscriber error-handling obligation to it.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a data stream FIN terminates in the middle of a serialized Object.
requirements.rationale: The recommendation is for the Object receiver. It covers graceful truncation, not reset streams, and does not mandate the same response from a publisher lacking an incoming subscription or FETCH.

requirements.summary: Do not have more than one stream open at a time with the same Subgroup Header field values.
requirements.rationale: Actual simultaneous openness is sender transport state. The listener can receive a new header before a delayed FIN or reset on another stream even when the sender closed that stream first; receiver arrival order cannot prove sender overlap.

requirements.summary: Cancel a non-control unidirectional data stream for congestion or another reason without terminating its subscription.
